description: tif_pixarlog.c in libtiff 4.0.6 has out-of-bounds write vulnerabilities in heap allocated buffers. Reported as MSVR 35094, aka "PixarLog horizontalDifference heap-buffer-overflow."

code_evidence: The JPEG branch allocates buffer with t2p->tiff_datasize bytes and zeroes it, then copies count bytes from the JPEGTABLES field into buffer and advances bufferoffset by count-2 without validating count against tiff_datasize.

Each strip is processed via t2p_process_jpeg_strip, which appends data into buffer at bufferoffset; afterward lines 256-257 unconditionally write two EOI bytes at buffer[bufferoffset++], with no remaining-capacity check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs heap writes indexed by bufferoffset into a buffer whose size is fixed at tiff_datasize, and the missing bounds check allows writes beyond that allocation, matching CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). It is not merely an integer overflow; the concrete failure is a write past the buffer end.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: buffer is sized to t2p->tiff_datasize, but the JPEGTABLES copy (count) and per-strip appends advance bufferoffset without ensuring it stays within that allocation. A crafted TIFF with an oversized JPEGTABLES count or strip data drives bufferoffset past tiff_datasize; the write to buffer[bufferoffset++] then writes past the heap buffer, corrupting memory.

commit_msg:
vmx does not restore GDT.LIMIT to the host value, instead it sets it to 64KB.
This means host userspace can learn a few bits of host memory.

Fix by reloading GDTR when we load other host state.

Signed-off-by: Avi Kivity <avi@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Marcelo Tosatti <mtosatti@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tload_gdt(&__get_cpu_var(host_gdt));']}
description: A flaw was found in Linux kernel's KVM virtualization subsystem. The VMX code does not restore the GDT.LIMIT to the previous host value, but instead sets it to 64KB. With a corrupted GDT limit a host's userspace code has an ability to place malicious entries in the GDT, particularly to the per-cpu variables. An attacker can use this to escalate their privileges.

code_evidence: __vmx_load_host_state restores FS/GS/LDT selectors, host GS base and TSS, but never reloads the host GDTR; the pre-patch function ends after reload_tss() and the FPU clts() with no load_gdt call.
The commit adds load_gdt(&__get_cpu_var(host_gdt)) to this same function, confirming the missing GDTR restoration is localized here.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The omission leaves the host GDT resource in an incorrect, guest-influenced state rather than its expected host value, i.e., improper initialization/restoration of a resource before use. This matches CWE-665; it is not an out-of-bounds or type-confusion issue but a failure to re-establish expected resource state.

evidence_lines.code: reload_tss();

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: When returning to host context after guest execution, the function restores several host segment and descriptor-table states but omits reloading GDT.LIMIT, leaving the guest-set 64KB limit active. Host userspace then operates with a corrupted GDT limit, enabling placement of malicious GDT entries targeting per-cpu data and privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
Fix invalid memory accesses and add missing checks in src/dtm.cpp

There are several issues when loading .dtm files which can lead
to invalid memory accesses. This patch fixes the following:

* In CdtmLoader::load(), ensure that title and author strings
  are properly terminated to avoid out-of-bounds reads.
* Check that the number of instruments is valid. This avoids a
  heap-based buffer overflow (see issue #86).
* Reading the description string could overflow a stack buffer
  by 1 byte and write past the end of the array into an adjacent
  class member (which is only initialized later). Get rid of the
  stack buffer and truncate the description if necessary.
* Fail loading when an error is detected while trying to read
  data from the file or while decoding RLE data.
* Check the argument of CdtmLoader::getinstrument() to avoid
  out-of-bound accesses.

This fixes CVE-2019-14691.

Fixes: https://github.com/adplug/adplug/issues/86

description: AdPlug 2.3.1 has a heap-based buffer overflow in CdtmLoader::load() in dtm.cpp.

code_evidence: Per iteration, bufstr_length is read from the file; the check only rejects values >80, so 80 is accepted. readString fills bufstr[0..79], then bufstr[bufstr_length]=0 writes bufstr[80], one byte past the 80-byte local array bufstr.
bufstr is a fixed 80-byte stack buffer while desc is a separate fixed 1280-byte array; the NUL terminator write at index equal to the length is the out-of-bounds write.

commit_msg:
BUG/MAJOR: htx: fix missing header name length check in htx_add_header/trailer

Ori Hollander of JFrog Security reported that htx_add_header() and
htx_add_trailer() were missing a length check on the header name. While
this does not allow to overwrite any memory area, it results in bits of
the header name length to slip into the header value length and may
result in forging certain header names on the input. The sad thing here
is that a FIXME comment was present suggesting to add the required length
checks :-(

The injected headers are visible to the HTTP internals and to the config
rules, so haproxy will generally stay synchronized with the server. But
there is one exception which is the content-length header field, because
it is already deduplicated on the input, but before being indexed. As
such, injecting a content-length header after the deduplication stage
may be abused to present a different, shorter one on the other side and
help build a request smuggling attack, or even maybe a response splitting
attack. CVE-2021-40346 was assigned to this problem.

As a mitigation measure, it is sufficient to verify that no more than
one such header is present in any message, which is normally the case
thanks to the duplicate checks:

   http-request  deny if { req.hdr_cnt(content-length) gt 1 }
   http-response deny if { res.hdr_cnt(content-length) gt 1 }

This must be backported to all HTX-enabled versions, hence as far as 2.0.
In 2.3 and earlier, the functions are in src/htx.c instead.

Many thanks to Ori for his work and his responsible report!
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t/* FIXME: check name.len (< 256B) and value.len (< 1MB) */'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (name.len > 255 || value.len > 1048575)', '\t\treturn NULL;', '']}
description: An integer overflow exists in HAProxy 2.0 through 2.5 in htx_add_header that can be exploited to perform an HTTP request smuggling attack, allowing an attacker to bypass all configured http-request HAProxy ACLs and possibly other ACLs.

code_evidence: Line 5 passes the sum name.len + value.len to htx_add_blk() as the block size without bounding either component. Line 8 then packs the lengths into blk->info as (value.len << 8) + name.len, so an oversized name.len spills into the value-length field.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the defect is unchecked integer arithmetic on attacker-controlled lengths (name.len + value.len and the <<8 packing) whose result is assumed valid. The commit explicitly adds bounds (name.len > 255, value.len > 1048575) to prevent the wraparound; the consequence is logic/access-control bypass, an allowed impact of integer overflow.

evidence_lines.code:
blk = htx_add_blk(htx, HTX_BLK_HDR, name.len + value.len);
blk->info += (value.len << 8) + name.len;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function never constrains name.len or value.len before combining them, so the length arithmetic and the packed info field can overflow/wrap. Trigger: a crafted header with a name length exceeding 255 (or a very large value) is added. The wrapped size/field allows forged header names to be indexed, enabling content-length injection and request smuggling rather than a direct memory overwrite.

commit_msg:
Correctly load/initialize classes when using ConstantPool

- do not load classes in the "ifLoaded" calls
- never intitialize classes in the natives
- do not update the constant pool when querying from the natives

Fixes: #12016

[ci skip]

Signed-off-by: Graham Chapman <graham_chapman@ca.ibm.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\tmethod = vmFunctions->resolveStaticMethodRef(vmThread, constantPool, cpIndex, resolveFlags);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tresolveFlags |= (J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_THROW_ON_FAIL | J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_CLASS_INIT | J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_CP_UPDATE);', '\t\t\t\t\tmethod = vmFunctions->resolveStaticMethodRefInto(vmThread, constantPool, cpIndex, resolveFlags, NULL);']}
description: In Eclipse Openj9 to version 0.25.0, usage of the jdk.internal.reflect.ConstantPool API causes the JVM in some cases to pre-resolve certain constant pool entries. This allows a user to call static methods or access static members without running the class initialization method, and may allow a user to observe uninitialized values.

code_evidence: resolveFlags is used unchanged when getRAMConstantRefAndType and later resolveStaticMethodRef are invoked; no J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_CLASS_INIT is applied here.
For a static-method constant, the code calls resolveStaticMethodRef with the caller-supplied resolveFlags, which can permit class initialization during resolution.
The resolved method is then converted via getJNIMethodID and exposed through ToReflectedMethod, making the method reachable by the caller.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-909 covers missing initialization of a critical resource; here the class-initialization resource is not guaranteed before the static method is resolved and exposed. This is distinct from a mere incorrect constant-pool update, which is a resolution-state issue rather than missing initialization.

evidence_lines.code:
vmFunctions->internalEnterVMFromJNI(vmThread);
result = getRAMConstantRefAndType(vmThread, constantPoolOop, cpIndex, &cpType, &ramConstantRef);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the reflection path resolves a static method reference without forcing a no-class-init flag, so resolution may initialize the class or expose a method whose class initialization has not run. Trigger: a caller using the ConstantPool API on a static-method entry. Consequence: static methods/members can be reached before class initialization, allowing observation of uninitialized values.

description: An information disclosure vulnerability in lvm/wrapper/Bundle/EffectBundle.cpp in libeffects in the Qualcomm audio post processor could enable a local malicious application to access data outside of its permission levels. This issue is rated as Moderate because it could be used to access sensitive data without permission. Product: Android. Versions: 5.0.2, 5.1.1, 6.0, 6.0.1, 7.0, 7.1. Android ID: A-32588756.

EQ_PARAM_BAND_FREQ_RANGE likewise forwards a negative param2 to EqualizerGetBandFreqRange, which writes results into pValue based on the invalid band index.

description: A flaw was found in Binutils. A logic fail in the bfd_init_section_decompress_status function may lead to the use of an uninitialized variable that can cause a crash and local denial of service.

In the compression_header_size == 0 branch (zlib-gnu), only uncompressed_size is set at line 30 and ch_type is never assigned before the branch closes at line 31. ch_type is then read at lines 50-51 to choose DECOMPRESS_SECTION_ZSTD vs DECOMPRESS_SECTION_ZLIB.

commit_msg:
Fix off-by-one bounds check on CHM PMGI/PMGL chunk numbers and
reject empty filenames. Thanks to Hanno Böck for reporting
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (chunk_num > chm->num_chunks) return NULL;'], 'added_lines': ['    if (chunk_num >= chm->num_chunks) return NULL;']}
description: An issue was discovered in mspack/chmd.c in libmspack before 0.7alpha. There is an off-by-one error in the CHM PMGI/PMGL chunk number validity checks, which could lead to denial of service (uninitialized data dereference and application crash).

code_evidence: Line 8 validates chunk_num with `> chm->num_chunks`, permitting chunk_num == num_chunks even though valid indices are 0..num_chunks-1.
The cache is sized to num_chunks entries (line 10) and zeroed (line 15), then indexed by chunk_num at line 17 without a further bound check.
Line 22 computes the seek offset using the out-of-range chunk_num, and line 24 seeks to it before reading.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a classic off-by-one: the comparison uses an incorrect maximum value, allowing an index one past the valid range. This matches CWE-193 rather than a generic out-of-bounds write, since the defect is the miscomputed boundary in the check.

evidence_lines.code: if (chunk_num > chm->num_chunks) return NULL;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the incorrect maximum bound: the check should reject chunk_num >= num_chunks, but `>` admits the one-past-end value. The trigger is a caller passing chunk_num equal to num_chunks; the function then indexes the cache array out of bounds and seeks/reads past the chunk region, yielding uninitialized-data dereference or a crash (DoS).

description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. The implementation of `tf.raw_ops.SdcaOptimizer` triggers undefined behavior due to dereferencing a null pointer. The implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/60a45c8b6192a4699f2e2709a2645a751d435cc3/tensorflow/core/kernels/sdca_internal.cc) does not validate that the user supplied arguments satisfy all constraints expected by the op(https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/raw_ops/SdcaOptimizer). Consequence: the loop iterates past the sparse_indices list and dereferences an invalid/absent tensor, yielding undefined behavior (the reported null-pointer dereference).

description: A flaw was found in the Linux Kernel in versions after 4.5-rc1 in the way mremap handled DAX Huge Pages. This flaw allows a local attacker with access to a DAX enabled storage to escalate their privileges on the system.

code_evidence: Line 26 gates the huge-PMD handling path on only is_swap_pmd or pmd_trans_huge; a DAX/devmap huge PMD (PAGE_PSE|PAGE_DEVMAP) is neither, so it falls to the else branch.
Line 41 treats the entry as a normal PMD only when extent == PMD_SIZE, then line 54 allocates a PTE table and line 59 moves PTEs through it, interpreting devmap huge-PMD memory as a page-table page.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The same PMD memory is classified by one type (normal PMD/PTE table) while its actual type is a DAX devmap huge page, and operations on it assume incompatible layout—type confusion. Contrast with CWE-787: the write is a consequence of the misclassification, not the primary flaw; the missing pmd_devmap check is the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the huge-PMD predicate omits pmd_devmap, so a DAX-mapped huge PMD is handled as an ordinary page-table PMD. Trigger: mremap over a DAX nvdimm mapping with a full PMD-sized extent. Consequence: move_ptes walks and rewrites memory interpreted as PTE entries rather than the huge mapping, corrupting page tables/memory and enabling privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
When the 'v->config_ctx' eventfd_ctx reference is released we didn't
set it to NULL. So if the same character device (e.g. /dev/vhost-vdpa-0)
is re-opened, the 'v->config_ctx' is invalid and calling again
vhost_vdpa_config_put() causes use-after-free issues like the
following refcount_t underflow:

    refcount_t: underflow; use-after-free.
    WARNING: CPU: 2 PID: 872 at lib/refcount.c:28 refcount_warn_saturate+0xae/0xf0
    RIP: 0010:refcount_warn_saturate+0xae/0xf0
    Call Trace:
     eventfd_ctx_put+0x5b/0x70
     vhost_vdpa_release+0xcd/0x150 [vhost_vdpa]
     __fput+0x8e/0x240
     ____fput+0xe/0x10
     task_work_run+0x66/0xa0
     exit_to_user_mode_prepare+0x118/0x120
     syscall_exit_to_user_mode+0x21/0x50
     ? __x64_sys_close+0x12/0x40
     do_syscall_64+0x45/0x50
     entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x44/0xae

Fixes: 776f395004d8 ("vhost_vdpa: Support config interrupt in vdpa")
Cc: lingshan.zhu@intel.com
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Stefano Garzarella <sgarzare@redhat.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210311135257.109460-2-sgarzare@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Michael S. Tsirkin <mst@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Zhu Lingshan <lingshan.zhu@intel.com>
Acked-by: Jason Wang <jasowang@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (v->config_ctx)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (v->config_ctx) {', '\t\tv->config_ctx = NULL;', '\t}']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.11.9. drivers/vhost/vdpa.c has a use-after-free because v->config_ctx has an invalid value upon re-opening a character device, aka CID-f6bbf0010ba0.

code_evidence: The function checks v->config_ctx and, if non-NULL, calls eventfd_ctx_put() to release the eventfd reference, but it never resets v->config_ctx to NULL afterward. The stale pointer remains in the vhost_vdpa structure.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code references memory that has already been freed because the pointer is not cleared after release, matching CWE-416. This is a stale-pointer reuse, distinct from a simple NULL-check omission; the missing assignment to NULL is what enables the use-after-free.

evidence_lines.code:
if (v->config_ctx)
eventfd_ctx_put(v->config_ctx);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: releasing the eventfd_ctx reference leaves v->config_ctx holding a dangling pointer. Trigger: the same character device is re-opened, and vhost_vdpa_config_put() runs again on the stale field. Consequence: eventfd_ctx_put() operates on freed memory, producing a refcount underflow/use-after-free (crash or memory corruption), as the commit message reports.

commit_msg:
vhost: fix FD leak with inflight messages

Even if unlikely, a buggy vhost-user master might attach fds to inflight
messages. Add checks like for other types of vhost-user messages.

Fixes: d87f1a1cb7b6 ("vhost: support inflight info sharing")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: David Marchand <david.marchand@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Maxime Coquelin <maxime.coquelin@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (validate_msg_fds(dev, ctx, 0) != 0)', '\t\treturn RTE_VHOST_MSG_RESULT_ERR;']}
description: A flaw was found in dpdk. This flaw allows a malicious vhost-user master to attach an unexpected number of fds as ancillary data to VHOST_USER_GET_INFLIGHT_FD / VHOST_USER_SET_INFLIGHT_FD messages that are not closed by the vhost-user slave. By sending such messages continuously, the vhost-user master exhausts available fd in the vhost-user slave process, leading to a denial of service.

code_evidence: The function validates only the message size (ctx->msg.size) and then proceeds to allocate inflight memory and set ctx->fds[0] = fd and ctx->fd_num = 1 without checking how many ancillary fds the vhost-user master actually attached to the request.
Any fds supplied by the master beyond the single expected fd are never examined or closed by this handler, so they persist in the process.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the handler fails to control a limited OS resource (file descriptors) and does not throttle or reject excessive resource-bearing requests; the resulting consumption of process fds directly enables DoS. This is resource exhaustion from missing input constraint validation rather than a memory-safety defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the message handler accepts a request without validating the attached fd count, so unexpected ancillary fds are neither consumed nor closed. Trigger: a malicious vhost-user master repeatedly sends GET_INFLIGHT_FD/SET_INFLIGHT_FD messages attaching extra fds. Consequence: the slave process accumulates open file descriptors until exhaustion, causing denial of service.

commit_msg:
Fix memory leak

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/issues/131
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['             matvar->internal->num_fields > 0 ) {'], 'added_lines': ['            matvar->internal->num_fields > 0 ) {']}
description: A memory leak was discovered in Mat_VarCalloc in mat.c in matio 1.5.17 because SafeMulDims does not consider the rank==0 case.

code_evidence: When matvar->dims is non-NULL, nelems is initialized to 1 and then passed to SafeMulDims(matvar, &nelems); the dims buffer is freed afterward, but nelems is not corrected for the rank==0 case.

For MAT_C_STRUCT with mem_conserve unset, fields is cast from matvar->data and the loop bound is computed via SafeMul(&nelems_x_nfields, nelems, matvar->internal->num_fields); if nelems is wrong, the loop frees the wrong number of field pointers before free(matvar->data).
For MAT_C_CELL, the loop iterates i < nelems and calls Mat_VarFree(cells[i]) for each element before free(matvar->data); an incorrect nelems causes incorrect traversal of the cells array.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because the function fails to release all allocated memory associated with struct fields or cell elements after their effective lifetime; the defect is incomplete release, not a use-after-free or overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: SafeMulDims does not handle rank==0, so nelems computed from dims is not adjusted for empty/zero-rank variables. Trigger: freeing a struct or cell whose dims lead to a mismatched nelems count. Consequence: Mat_VarFree traverses the wrong number of elements, leaving some allocated field/cell entries unreleased, a memory leak (and potential instability).

commit_msg:
Check that ecall [user_check] pointers and ocall_malloc result pointer are outside enclave (#67)

This should reduce the enclave's attack surface by preventing an attacker from invoking ecalls on or triggering unexpected writes to arbitrary enclave memory, which could potentially leak information about that memory or lead to incorrect results.

Fixes #36. Fixes #66.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  // Guard against operating on arbitrary enclave memory', '  assert(sgx_is_outside_enclave(input_rows, input_rows_length) == 1);', '  sgx_lfence();', '']}
description: An issue was discovered in UC Berkeley RISE Opaque before 2018-12-01. There is no boundary check on ocall_malloc. The return value could be a pointer to enclave memory. It could cause an arbitrary enclave memory write.

code_evidence: The ecall accepts caller-supplied input_rows and input_rows_length and passes them directly to scan_collect_last_primary without verifying that input_rows points outside the enclave; the only guard is the try/catch, which does not validate pointer provenance.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing boundary/provenance check allows operations on memory outside the intended caller buffer, enabling writes past the intended buffer region; CWE-787 captures such out-of-bounds writes. It is not merely a logic error because the unchecked pointer/length can cause memory writes beyond the intended buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the ecall trusts an attacker-controlled pointer/length pair and forwards it into an internal routine that reads and writes based on it. Trigger: an attacker invokes the ecall with input_rows pointing into enclave memory. Consequence: unintended reads or writes to arbitrary enclave memory, potentially leaking enclave data or corrupting results, consistent with an out-of-bounds memory access driven by unvalidated bounds.

description: epan/dissectors/packet-ipmi-trace.c in the IPMI trace dissector in Wireshark 2.x before 2.0.6 does not properly consider whether a string is constant, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (use-after-free and application crash) via a crafted packet.

Also memset ps_dec_op structure to zero.

description: The H.264 decoder in mediaserver in Android 6.x before 2016-07-01 does not initialize certain slice data, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (memory corruption) via a crafted media file, aka internal bug 28165661.

code_evidence: On the error-concealment path (prev_slice_err==1), the code calls ih264d_start_of_pic with ps_dec->ps_cur_slice fields (u2_frame_num, and downstream u1_field_pic_flag/u1_slice_type/u1_nal_ref_idc) that were never initialized for this crafted-error flow; the patch adds explicit zeroing assignments before the call.

Trigger: a crafted H.264 media file causing prev_slice_err==1. Consequence: inconsistent slice state drives ih264d_start_of_pic and deblocking/parse paths into memory corruption, enabling code execution or DoS.

commit_msg:
usbip_host updates device status without holding lock from stub probe,
disconnect and rebind code paths. When multiple requests to import a
device are received, these unprotected code paths step all over each
other and drive fails with NULL-ptr deref and use-after-free errors.

The driver uses a table lock to protect the busid array for adding and
deleting busids to the table. However, the probe, disconnect and rebind
paths get the busid table entry and update the status without holding
the busid table lock. Add a new finer grain lock to protect the busid
entry. This new lock will be held to search and update the busid entry
fields from get_busid_idx(), add_match_busid() and del_match_busid().

match_busid_show() does the same to access the busid entry fields.

get_busid_priv() changed to return the pointer to the busid entry holding
the busid lock. stub_probe(), stub_disconnect() and stub_device_rebind()
call put_busid_priv() to release the busid lock before returning. This
changes fixes the unprotected code paths eliminating the race conditions
in updating the busid entries.

Reported-by: Jakub Jirasek
Signed-off-by: Shuah Khan (Samsung OSG) <shuah@kernel.org>
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tfor (i = 0; i < MAX_BUSID; i++)'], 'added_lines': ['\tfor (i = 0; i < MAX_BUSID; i++) {', '\t\tspin_lock(&busid_table[i].busid_lock);', '\t\tspin_unlock(&busid_table[i].busid_lock);', '\t}']}
description: In the Linux Kernel before version 4.16.11, 4.14.43, 4.9.102, and 4.4.133, multiple race condition errors when handling probe, disconnect, and rebind operations can be exploited to trigger a use-after-free condition or a NULL pointer dereference by sending multiple USB over IP packets.

code_evidence: match_busid_show() acquires only the coarse busid_table_lock, then iterates over busid_table[i] and reads name[0] and name at lines 7-8 without any per-entry busid_lock. The patch adds spin_lock/spin_unlock(&busid_table[i].busid_lock) around each entry, confirming that the pre-patch loop reads entry fields with no exclusive access relative to probe/disconnect/rebind paths that modify the same entries.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a concurrent read of a shared resource (the busid_table entry) that lacks exclusive synchronization with writers, matching CWE-362's timing-window/exclusivity violation. This is a race condition rather than a simple missing-lock on a single non-shared variable, since an interfering code sequence accesses the same entry.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the read loop accesses busid_table[i].name while the probe, disconnect, and rebind code paths update the same entry fields without a common lock. Trigger: concurrent import/rebind requests modify an entry while match_busid_show() reads it. Supported consequence: a race condition that can produce inconsistent reads and, per the commit, NULL-pointer dereference or use-after-free crashes.

description: Divide By Zero in vim/vim from 9.0.1367-1 to 9.0.1367-3

code_evidence: width1 is computed as curwin->w_width - curwin_col_off(); width2 is then width1 + curwin_col_off2(). When width1 is non-positive, width2 can be zero, and line 106 divides (curwin->w_skipcol - width1) by width2 without checking width2 != 0.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-369 fits because the code performs an integer division where the divisor width2 can evaluate to zero due to unvalidated window dimensions. This is a direct divide-by-zero, not merely an out-of-bounds or arithmetic overflow issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the divisor width2 is derived from window width minus column offsets and is never validated before division. Trigger: a narrow window (e.g. with 'smoothscroll' set) makes width1 negative and width2 zero while w_skipcol > width1. Consequence: integer division by zero crashes Vim (DoS).

commit_msg:
IxVeriWave: Adjust signature timestamp checking.

Move the signature timestamp bounds checks inside get_signature_ts. Fix
what appears to be an off-by-one error.

Manually backported from 5dbc1d8d1c.

Bug: 14297
Change-Id: I6455162d12fd0854ffe6daaf624eeaf94f6e32b0
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/25246
Petri-Dish: Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
Tested-by: Petri Dish Buildbot
Reviewed-by: Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if ((m_ptr[sig_off] == 0xdd) && (sig_off + 15 <= (rec_size - vVW510021_W_STATS_TRAILER_LEN)))', '        sig_ts = get_signature_ts(m_ptr, sig_off);'], 'added_lines': ['    if (m_ptr[sig_off] == 0xdd)', '        sig_ts = get_signature_ts(m_ptr, sig_off, rec_size - vVW510021_W_STATS_TRAILER_LEN);']}
description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.3 and 2.2.0 to 2.2.11, the IxVeriWave file parser could crash. This was addressed in wiretap/vwr.c by correcting the signature timestamp bounds checks.

code_evidence: find_signature returns sig_off, then m_ptr[sig_off] is dereferenced at line 151. In the vulnerable version the bounds check (sig_off + 15 <= rec_size - trailer) is combined with the 0xdd test, so the dereference itself is not guarded against sig_off exceeding the buffer.
get_signature_ts reads a timestamp at m_ptr + sig_off without knowing the record size; the check was only done at the caller and used an off-by-one bound.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs reads through m_ptr[sig_off] and get_signature_ts using an offset not properly constrained to the buffer's intended boundary, which is exactly out-of-bounds memory access within a buffer (CWE-119). The off-by-one check is a missing bounds constraint rather than a different weakness class.

evidence_lines.code:
sig_off = find_signature(m_ptr, rec_size - 20, pay_off, flow_id, flow_seq);
if ((m_ptr[sig_off] == 0xdd) && (sig_off + 15 <= (rec_size - vVW510021_W_STATS_TRAILER_LEN)))

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the signature offset returned by find_signature is used to index/read m_ptr without a correct upper-bound constraint on sig_off relative to the record size. Trigger: a crafted IxVeriWave record whose signature location or flow fields cause find_signature to return an offset at/near the end of the buffer. Consequence: out-of-bounds read (m_ptr[sig_off] and the timestamp read), leading to crash/DoS as described.

Use MAKERNOTE length as data size.

description: exif_process_IFD_in_MAKERNOTE in ext/exif/exif.c in PHP before 5.6.37, 7.0.x before 7.0.31, 7.1.x before 7.1.20, and 7.2.x before 7.2.8 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read and application crash) via a crafted JPEG file.

code_evidence: Line 62 sets offset_base = value_ptr + offset_diff in the MN_OFFSET_GUESS branch, but the loop at lines 72-74 still passes the original IFDlength (not the remaining length value_len - offset_diff) to exif_process_IFD_TAG. The bounds check at line 68 uses value_len, yet the callee receives a length that can exceed the actual buffer remaining after offset_base is advanced.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function passes an oversized length relative to the shifted buffer base into a read routine, directly enabling reads beyond the intended buffer, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). It is a read overrun, not a write, so CWE-787 does not apply.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: when offset_diff > 0, offset_base is advanced past value_ptr but IFDlength is not reduced, so the callee believes more data is available than actually exists. Trigger: a crafted JPEG maker note with MN_OFFSET_GUESS and a positive offset_diff. Consequence: exif_process_IFD_TAG reads past the end of the value buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read and crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
When setting up the next segment, we check what type the iter is and
handle it accordingly. However, when incrementing and processed amount
we do not, and both iter advance and addr/len are adjusted, regardless
of type. Split the increment side just like we do on the setup side.

Fixes: 4017eb91a9e7 ("io_uring: make loop_rw_iter() use original user supplied pointers")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: Valentina Palmiotti <vpalmiotti@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Pavel Begunkov <asml.silence@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\treq->rw.len -= nr;', '\t\treq->rw.addr += nr;', '\t\tiov_iter_advance(iter, nr);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!iov_iter_is_bvec(iter)) {', '\t\t\tiov_iter_advance(iter, nr);', '\t\t} else {', '\t\t\treq->rw.len -= nr;', '\t\t\treq->rw.addr += nr;', '\t\t}']}
description: loop_rw_iter in fs/io_uring.c in the Linux kernel 5.10 through 5.14.6 allows local users to gain privileges by using IORING_OP_PROVIDE_BUFFERS to trigger a free of a kernel buffer, as demonstrated by using /proc/<pid>/maps for exploitation.

code_evidence: When iter is a bvec, iovec is built from req->rw.addr/len instead of the iterator; otherwise iov_iter_iovec(iter) is used.

After a short/normal transfer, nr is unconditionally added to ret, then req->rw.len/addr are decremented/incremented and iov_iter_advance(iter, nr) is called even for bvec iterators, where the iterator itself was never the source of the iovec.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-763 fits because the code releases/advances the wrong resource (the iterator) for bvec iterators while the intended adjustment is req->rw.addr/len, i.e., the release/advance operation is applied to an incompatible object. This is not merely a length-calculation bug; the incorrect destination of the advance causes the invalid release.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: setup distinguishes bvec iterators (adjust req->rw.addr/len) from non-bvec iterators (adjust iter), but the increment path applies both adjustments unconditionally. Trigger: a bvec iterator whose iovec comes from req->rw.addr/len; after a completed transfer, iov_iter_advance also mutates the iterator, so addr/len and iterator state diverge and later iterations use inconsistent pointers/lengths. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds access or freeing of a kernel buffer, enabling memory corruption or privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
_bfd_clear_contents bounds checking

This PR shows a fuzzed binary triggering a segfault via a bad
relocation in .debug_line.  It turns out that unlike normal
relocations applied to a section, the linker applies those with
symbols from discarded sections via _bfd_clear_contents without
checking that the relocation is within the section bounds.  The same
thing now happens when reading debug sections since commit
a4cd947aca23, the PR23425 fix.

	PR 23770
	PR 23425
	* reloc.c (_bfd_clear_contents): Replace "location" param with
	"buf" and "off".  Bounds check "off".  Return status.
	* cofflink.c (_bfd_coff_generic_relocate_section): Update
	_bfd_clear_contents call.
	* elf-bfd.h (RELOC_AGAINST_DISCARDED_SECTION): Likewise.
	* elf32-arc.c (elf_arc_relocate_section): Likewise.
	* elf32-i386.c (elf_i386_relocate_section): Likewise.
	* elf32-metag.c (metag_final_link_relocate): Likewise.
	* elf32-nds32.c (nds32_elf_get_relocated_section_contents): Likewise.
	* elf32-ppc.c (ppc_elf_relocate_section): Likewise.
	* elf32-visium.c (visium_elf_relocate_section): Likewise.
	* elf64-ppc.c (ppc64_elf_relocate_section): Likewise.
	* elf64-x86-64.c *(elf_x86_64_relocate_section): Likewise.
	* libbfd-in.h (_bfd_clear_contents): Update prototype.
	* libbfd.h: Regenerate.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t       contents + rel->r_offset);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t       contents, rel->r_offset);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Binary File Descriptor (BFD) library (aka libbfd), as distributed in GNU Binutils 2.31. An invalid memory address dereference was discovered in read_reloc in reloc.c. The vulnerability causes a segmentation fault and application crash, which leads to denial of service, as demonstrated by objdump, because of missing _bfd_clear_contents bounds checking.

code_evidence: When the relocation's symbol resolves to a discarded section, the code calls _bfd_clear_contents with the raw contents pointer plus rel->r_offset, without validating that r_offset stays within input_section's bounds before the buffer is accessed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a memory write at contents + r_offset beyond the section buffer, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds buffer operation. The missing constraint is the offset validation; the crash is the resultant consequence rather than the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a relocation r_offset from an untrusted object file is added to the section contents buffer and passed to _bfd_clear_contents, which zeroes memory at that offset with no bounds check. Trigger: a crafted relocation whose symbol lies in a discarded section. Consequence: an out-of-bounds write/dereference causing a segmentation fault and denial of service.

commit_msg: fs: Don't try to delete the file when copying. It could cause a security issue if the file exists and doesn't allow other's to read/write. delete could allow someone to create the file and have access to the data.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ["\t/* We're going to create/open/truncate the new file, then as we read the contents from the old file we'll write it", ' \t * to new file. */', '\tif (M_fs_perms_can_access(path_new, M_FS_PERMS_MODE_NONE) == M_FS_ERROR_SUCCESS) {', "\t\t/* Try to delete the file since we'll be overwrite it. This is so when we create the file we create it without", " \t\t * any permissions and to ensure that anything that has the file already open won't be able to read the new", "\t\t * contents we're writing to the file or be able to change the perms. There is an unavoidable race condition", '\t\t * between deleting and creating the file where someone could create the file and have access. However,', '\t\t * depending on the OS they may have access even if the file is created with no perms... */', '\t\tres = M_fs_delete(path_new, M_FALSE, NULL, M_FS_PROGRESS_NOEXTRA);', '\t\tif (res != M_FS_ERROR_SUCCESS) {', '\t\t\treturn res;', '\t\t}', '\t}'], 'added_lines': ['', "\t/* We're going to create/open/truncate the new file, then as we read the contents from the old file we'll write it", '\t * to new file. */']}
description: mstdlib (aka the M Standard Library for C) 1.2.0 has incorrect file access control in situations where M_fs_perms_can_access attempts to delete an existing file (that lacks public read/write access) during a copy operation, related to fs/m_fs.c and fs/m_fs_path.c. An attacker could create the file and then would have access to the data.

code_evidence: Before opening path_new for writing, the function checks whether the destination is accessible and then deletes it via M_fs_delete; this creates a window in which no file exists at path_new.
The destination is subsequently opened with M_FS_FILE_MODE_WRITE|M_FS_FILE_MODE_OVERWRITE, so permissions depend on the delete/recreate sequence rather than solely on the supplied perms.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's handling of the destination resource lets an unintended actor obtain read/write access to the copied data because the delete/recreate step permits attacker-controlled permission assignment, matching CWE-732 (incorrect permission assignment for a critical resource). It is not merely a missing authorization check; the weakness is the resulting permissive access to the destination file.

evidence_lines.code: res = M_fs_file_open(&fd_new, path_new, M_FS_BUF_SIZE, M_FS_FILE_MODE_WRITE|M_FS_FILE_MODE_OVERWRITE, perms);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The delete-then-create sequence at [12-17] followed by the overwrite open at [30] leaves path_new absent between the two calls. An attacker who can create files in the directory can race in and create path_new with permissive permissions; the copy then writes sensitive data into the attacker-controlled file, exposing or allowing modification of the copied content.

When loads of devices are discovered a config file which is too large

This limits the number of config entries for unpaired devices which

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '  btif_config_devcache_cleanup();']}
description: btif_config.c in Bluetooth in Android 6.x before 2016-03-01 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory corruption and persistent daemon crash) by triggering a large number of configuration entries, and consequently exceeding the maximum size of a configuration file, aka internal bug 26071376.

commit_msg:
x86/vtx: Fix the checking for unknown/invalid MSR_DEBUGCTL bits

The VPMU_MODE_OFF early-exit in vpmu_do_wrmsr() introduced by c/s
11fe998e56 bypasses all reserved bit checking in the general case.  As a
result, a guest can enable BTS when it shouldn't be permitted to, and
lock up the entire host.

With vPMU active (not a security supported configuration, but useful for
debugging), the reserved bit checking in broken, caused by the original
BTS changeset 1a8aa75ed.

From a correctness standpoint, it is not possible to have two different
pieces of code responsible for different parts of value checking, if
there isn't an accumulation of bits which have been checked.  A
practical upshot of this is that a guest can set any value it
wishes (usually resulting in a vmentry failure for bad guest state).

Therefore, fix this by implementing all the reserved bit checking in the
main MSR_DEBUGCTL block, and removing all handling of DEBUGCTL from the
vPMU MSR logic.

This is XSA-269.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    {', '        /* Special handling for BTS */', '        if ( msr == MSR_IA32_DEBUGCTLMSR )', '        {', '            supported |= IA32_DEBUGCTLMSR_TR | IA32_DEBUGCTLMSR_BTS |', '                         IA32_DEBUGCTLMSR_BTINT;', '', '            if ( cpu_has(&current_cpu_data, X86_FEATURE_DSCPL) )', '                supported |= IA32_DEBUGCTLMSR_BTS_OFF_OS |', '                             IA32_DEBUGCTLMSR_BTS_OFF_USR;', '            if ( !(msr_content & ~supported) &&', '                 vpmu_is_set(vpmu, VPMU_CPU_HAS_BTS) )', '                return 0;', '            if ( (msr_content & supported) &&', '                 !vpmu_is_set(vpmu, VPMU_CPU_HAS_BTS) )', '                printk(XENLOG_G_WARNING', '                       "%pv: Debug Store unsupported on this CPU\\n",', '                       current);', '        }', '    }'], 'added_lines': []}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.11.x. The DEBUGCTL MSR contains several debugging features, some of which virtualise cleanly, but some do not. In particular, Branch Trace Store is not virtualised by the processor, and software has to be careful to configure it suitably not to lock up the core. As a result, it must only be available to fully trusted guests. Unfortunately, in the case that vPMU is disabled, all value checking was skipped, allowing the guest to choose any MSR_DEBUGCTL setting it likes. A malicious or buggy guest administrator (on Intel x86 HVM or PVH) can lock up the entire host, causing a Denial of Service.

code_evidence: When core2_vpmu_msr_common_check() returns false for MSR_IA32_DEBUGCTLMSR, the code computes a 'supported' mask of BTS-related bits [14,15,16,17,18] and returns 0 if all requested bits are within that mask and the vCPU has VPMU_CPU_HAS_BTS [19,20,21]. Otherwise it warns and falls through to return -EINVAL [28]. The check is only reached inside this branch; the accepted value is then written to the hardware MSR later at [148].
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function implements an authorization decision (which guest may set DEBUGCTL bits) via a mask/capability check, and the flaw is that this check can be skipped, permitting an action the guest should not be authorized to perform. That is an incorrect authorization check, matching CWE-863 rather than a pure input-validation issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The DEBUGCTL write is authorized by a bit-mask check that only passes when the guest's vPMU has BTS capability; the branch is the sole gate for DEBUGCTL. If this branch is bypassed (e.g., the earlier VPMU_MODE_OFF early-exit skips this function's checking), the guest-controlled msr_content reaches wrmsrl unchecked, letting an untrusted guest enable non-virtualized BTS and lock up the host.

commit_msg: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/1540
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    colormap_index=(ssize_t *) AcquireQuantumMemory(image->colors+1,', '      sizeof(*colormap_index));', '    colormap_index=(ssize_t *) AcquireQuantumMemory(MaxColormapSize+1,', '      sizeof(*colormap_index));'], 'added_lines': ['    colormap_index=(ssize_t *) AcquireQuantumMemory(MagickMax(image->colors+1,', '      MaxMap),sizeof(*colormap_index));', '    colormap_index=(ssize_t *) AcquireQuantumMemory(MagickMax(MaxColormapSize+1,', '      MaxMap),sizeof(*colormap_index));']}
description: In ImageMagick 7.0.8-40 Q16, there is a heap-based buffer over-read in the function WritePNMImage of coders/pnm.c, which allows an attacker to cause a denial of service or possibly information disclosure via a crafted image file. This is related to SetGrayscaleImage in MagickCore/quantize.c.

code_evidence: Colormap index buffer is allocated with only image->colors+1 (PseudoClass) or MaxColormapSize+1 elements; the memset at [31,32] writes MaxColormapSize entries, and the loop indexes colormap_index with ScaleQuantumToMap values and with image->colormap[i].alpha.
The allocation size is not raised to MaxMap, so the index array can be smaller than the intensity/alpha domain used to index it.
Intensity derived from pixel values is used as an index into colormap_index at [66,71,73,83] without ensuring it is below the allocated element count.
At [111] and [138,139] the alpha/index values index colormap_index, again without a bound check against the allocation size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads colormap_index at attacker-influenced indices beyond the allocated buffer, which is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The upstream fix enlarges the allocation to MagickMax(...,MaxMap), confirming the read past the buffer end; this is not a write overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the colormap_index array is allocated using image->colors+1 or MaxColormapSize+1 rather than a size covering the full index domain (MaxMap). Trigger: a crafted image whose grayscale intensity or stored index exceeds the allocated element count. Consequence: out-of-bounds reads of colormap_index, leading to crash (DoS) or potential information disclosure.

commit_msg:
[tflite] Validate segment ids for segment_sum.

Segment identifiers in segment_sum should be in a 1-D tensor of same size as the first dimension of the input. The values of the tensor should be integers from {0, 1, 2, ... k-1}, where k is the first dimension of the input. The segment identifiers must not contain jumps and must be increasing.

See https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/math#Segmentation as the source for these constraints.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 332510942
Change-Id: I898beaba00642c918bcd4b4d4ce893ebb190d869
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  int max_index = -1;', '  if (segment_id_size > 0) {', '    max_index = segment_ids->data.i32[segment_id_size - 1];'], 'added_lines': ['  // Segment ids should be of same cardinality as first input dimension and they', '  // should be increasing by at most 1, from 0 (e.g., [0, 0, 1, 2, 3] is valid)', '  TF_LITE_ENSURE_EQ(context, segment_id_size, data->dims->data[0]);', '  int previous_segment_id = -1;', '  for (int i = 0; i < segment_id_size; i++) {', '    const int current_segment_id = GetTensorData<int32_t>(segment_ids)[i];', '    if (i == 0) {', '      TF_LITE_ENSURE_EQ(context, current_segment_id, 0);', '    } else {', '      int delta = current_segment_id - previous_segment_id;', '      TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, delta == 0 || delta == 1);', '    }', '    previous_segment_id = current_segment_id;', '', '  const int max_index = previous_segment_id;', '']}
description: In TensorFlow Lite before versions 2.2.1 and 2.3.1, models using segment sum can trigger writes outside of bounds of heap allocated buffers by inserting negative elements in the segment ids tensor. Users having access to `segment_ids_data` can alter `output_index` and then write to outside of `output_data` buffer. This might result in a segmentation fault but it can also be used to further corrupt the memory and can be chained with other vulnerabilities to create more advanced exploits. The issue is patched in commit 204945b19e44b57906c9344c0d00120eeeae178a and is released in TensorFlow versions 2.2.1, or 2.3.1. A potential workaround would be to add a custom `Verifier` to the model loading code to ensure that the segment ids are all positive, although this only handles the case when the segment ids are stored statically in the model. A similar validation could be done if the segment ids are generated at runtime between inference steps. If the segment ids are generated as outputs of a tensor during inference steps, then there are no possible workaround and users are advised to upgrade to patched code.

code_evidence: The output's first dimension is derived solely from the last element of the segment ids tensor: max_index is set to segment_ids->data.i32[segment_id_size - 1] without validating that the ids are non-negative, start at 0, increase by at most 1, or match the input's first dimension.
That unchecked max_index is then used to size the output tensor via output_shape->data[0] = max_index + 1.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allows attacker-controlled segment ids to size a buffer that later receives indexed writes, directly enabling writes past the allocated buffer, matching CWE-787. It is not merely an integer issue (CWE-190); the missing validation causes an out-of-bounds write.

evidence_lines.code: output_shape->data[0] = max_index + 1;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the segment id values are trusted to define the output size. A negative or otherwise invalid id in segment_ids_data yields a small or negative max_index, producing an undersized output buffer; the subsequent segment-sum kernel writes at output_index derived from the same ids, landing outside the allocated output_data. Consequence: out-of-bounds heap write, potentially memory corruption or a crash.

commit_msg:
Fix FPE issue with `tf.raw_ops.FusedBatchNorm`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 370948185
Change-Id: If0c8e0320062ed6363e94ff5fe38e6a301f69ac2
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    OP_REQUIRES(', '        context, depth != 0,', '        errors::Internal("The 4th element in the input shape cannot be 0."));']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. An attacker can cause a denial of service via a FPE runtime error in `tf.raw_ops.FusedBatchNorm`. This is because the implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/828f346274841fa7505f7020e88ca36c22e557ab/tensorflow/core/kernels/fused_batch_norm_op.cc#L295-L297) performs a division based on the last dimension of the `x` tensor. Since this is controlled by the user, an attacker can trigger a denial of service. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Line 60 reads depth from the user-controlled 4th dimension of x. Line 62 computes rest_size = size / depth without first checking that depth is nonzero, so a zero-sized depth leads to integer division by zero.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function directly divides by a value (depth) that can be zero, matching CWE-369's divide-by-zero weakness. The fix adds an OP_REQUIRES check rejecting depth == 0, confirming the missing constraint on the divisor.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the division at line 62 uses depth as the divisor, but depth derives from the user-controlled input tensor shape. Trigger: supplying an x tensor whose 4th dimension is 0 causes the CPU FusedBatchNorm kernel to divide by zero, producing a floating-point exception that crashes the process (availability impact).

commit_msg:
fsck: fix out-of-bounds memory access

The size of utf16_name is ENTRY_NAME_MAX, we should pass
ENTRY_NAME_MAX to exfat_utf16_len(), not ENTRY_NAME_MAX*2.

exfat_utf16_enc() returns the length of the utf16-encoded
filename, it is not needed to call exfat_utf16_len().

Signed-off-by: Yuezhang Mo <Yuezhang.Mo@sony.com>
Signed-off-by: Namjae Jeon <linkinjeon@kernel.org>

description: exfatprogs before 1.2.2 allows out-of-bounds memory access, such as in read_file_dentry_set.

code_evidence: Lines 8 and 10-11 call memcmp on dentry->name_unicode with a length of strm_name_len * 2; strm_name_len is a caller-supplied stream name length that is not validated against the dentry's fixed name_unicode buffer size before the read.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is using an unvalidated or oversized length when scanning/copying fixed-size name buffers. Trigger occurs during dot/dotdot name repair when strm_name_len exceeds the dentry name buffer, or when exfat_utf16_len scans utf16_name up to ENTRY_NAME_MAX*2 bytes past its actual size. commit_msg:
net: fix infoleak in llc

The stack object “info” has a total size of 12 bytes. Its last byte
is padding which is not initialized and leaked via “put_cmsg”.

Signed-off-by: Kangjie Lu <kjlu@gatech.edu>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tmemset(&info, 0, sizeof(info));']}
description: The llc_cmsg_rcv function in net/llc/af_llc.c in the Linux kernel before 4.5.5 does not initialize a certain data structure, which allows attackers to obtain sensitive information from kernel stack memory by reading a message.

code_evidence: A stack-allocated struct llc_pktinfo info is declared at line 5 without initialization; only lpi_ifindex, lpi_sap and lpi_mac are assigned (lines 6-8), leaving trailing padding bytes uninitialized. Line 9 passes sizeof(info) bytes of this stack object to put_cmsg, copying the entire struct including the uninitialized padding to the caller's control message buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function explicitly transfers stale stack bytes into a message delivered to an unauthorized recipient, exposing sensitive kernel memory. This is a direct information exposure from insufficient initialization, matching CWE-200; the initialization defect is the cause and the disclosure is the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the stack object info is not zero-initialized before use, so padding bytes retain prior kernel stack contents. Trigger: a caller with LLC_CMSG_PKTINFO enabled receives a packet, causing llc_cmsg_rcv to copy the full struct via put_cmsg. Consequence: uninitialized kernel stack memory is disclosed to userspace.

In dcn*_create_resource_pool the allocated memory should be released if
construct pool fails.

Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com>

description: Memory leaks in *create_resource_pool() functions under drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc in the Linux kernel through 5.3.11 allow attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption). This affects the dce120_create_resource_pool() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce120/dce120_resource.c, the dce110_create_resource_pool() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce110/dce110_resource.c, the dce100_create_resource_pool() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce100/dce100_resource.c, the dcn10_create_resource_pool() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dcn10/dcn10_resource.c, and the dce112_create_resource_pool() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce112/dce112_resource.c, aka CID-104c307147ad.

code_evidence: Lines 5-6 allocate a dce110_resource_pool with kzalloc and store it in pool; lines 7-8 return NULL only when allocation fails.
Lines 9-10 return the embedded base on successful construct; when construct fails, lines 11-12 execute BREAK_TO_DEBUGGER and return NULL, abandoning the kzalloc'd pool without freeing it.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the failure path of construct() returns NULL without releasing the previously allocated pool. Trigger: construct(num_virtual_links, dc, pool) returns nonzero, so every call leaks one dce110_resource_pool. Repeated triggering consumes kernel memory, supporting denial of service via memory exhaustion.

description: epan/dissectors/packet-pktap.c in the Ethernet dissector in Wireshark 2.x before 2.0.4 mishandles the packet-header data type, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a crafted packet.

description: Net-SNMP through 5.8 has Improper Privilege Management because SNMP WRITE access to the EXTEND MIB provides the ability to run arbitrary commands as root.

MODE_SET_ACTION stores the SNMP-supplied command/args/input into the extension via netsnmp_strdup_and_null, so a remote SNMP write replaces the executable command string that the extend MIB later runs (as root).

in the case of 0x0.
invalid-vp80-00-comprehensive-018.ivf.2kf_0x6.ivf tests this case by
duplicating the first keyframe and additionally adds a valid one to
ensure decoding can resume without error.

description: A remote denial of service vulnerability in libvpx in Mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-11-01 could enable an attacker to use a specially crafted file to cause a device hang or reboot. This issue is rated as High due to the possibility of remote denial of service. Android ID: A-30593765.

code_evidence: Lines 16-19 cache the previous resolution (w,h) and call vp8_peek_si_internal on the attacker-controlled first fragment to populate ctx->si. Lines 26-27 set resolution_change only when the newly parsed width/height differ from the cached values, so an invalid keyframe that leaves ctx->si unchanged (or equal to a stale value) is treated as no resolution change.

Lines 66-71 show the setjmp error path taken when setjmp fires during buffer allocation; before the fix this path returned -1 without resetting ctx->si, so the cached resolution persisted for a subsequent decode of the same invalid keyframe.

commit_msg:
Fixed bugs of stack reallocation x GC

Macro 'checkstackGC' was doing a GC step after resizing the stack;
the GC could shrink the stack and undo the resize. Moreover, macro
'checkstackp' also does a GC step, which could remove the preallocated
CallInfo when calling a function. (Its name has been changed to
'checkstackGCp' to emphasize that it calls the GC.)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    checkstackp(L, nextra, where);  /* ensure stack space */'], 'added_lines': ['    checkstackGCp(L, nextra, where);  /* ensure stack space */']}
description: Lua through 5.4.0 mishandles the interaction between stack resizes and garbage collection, leading to a heap-based buffer overflow, heap-based buffer over-read, or use-after-free.

code_evidence: When wanted < 0, wanted is set to nextra and checkstackp(L, nextra, where) is called to ensure stack space for nextra extra arguments before L->top = where + nextra is assigned. The macro checkstackp performs a GC step after resizing; the GC can shrink the stack and undo the resize, so the subsequent top assignment and the writes in lines 9-12 (setobjs2s into where + i) may target space that is no longer allocated.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes stack slots after a check that GC can invalidate, so the writes can pass the end of the intended buffer, matching CWE-787. The weakness is the missing GC-safe constraint on the resize, not merely a memory disclosure.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the stack-growth check is not GC-safe, so a collection triggered during the check can reallocate/shrink the stack after the space was verified. Trigger: calling a vararg function with wanted < 0 and nextra large enough to force a stack resize. Consequence: subsequent writes to where + i can exceed the actual allocated stack, yielding a heap-based out-of-bounds write (or read/use-after-free).

This will prevent them creating top-frame navigations and is good practice anyway.

Lines 9-10 emit "will-navigate" and return nullptr when the listener cancels, but this is the only gate before delegating.

return nullptr;

The will-navigate emission is a cancellation hook rather than a validation constraint, so a cross-site top-frame navigation initiated by a sub-frame reaches the delegate and proceeds, bypassing the app's expected navigation restriction.

commit_msg:
PR22204, Lack of DW_LNE_end_sequence causes "infinite" loop

	PR 22204
	* dwarf2.c (decode_line_info): Ensure line_ptr stays within
	bounds in inner loop.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      while (! end_sequence)'], 'added_lines': ['      while (!end_sequence && line_ptr < line_end)']}
description: decode_line_info in dwarf2.c in the Binary File Descriptor (BFD) library (aka libbfd), as distributed in GNU Binutils 2.29, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (infinite loop) via a crafted ELF file.

code_evidence: The inner loop at [187-190] is guarded only by `! end_sequence`; `end_sequence` is set to 1 exclusively at line 228 inside the DW_LNE_end_sequence case.
The DW_LNE_end_sequence case [227-239] is the sole path that terminates the inner loop; if the crafted .debug_line data never contains this extended opcode, `end_sequence` stays 0.

The default extended-op case [282-289] jumps to line_fail and then fail, so malformed extended ops exit, but ordinary standard opcodes (e.g., DW_LNS_copy, DW_LNS_advance_pc) simply advance line_ptr without setting end_sequence.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The loop's exit condition (end_sequence) is unreachable for attacker-controlled input lacking DW_LNE_end_sequence, matching CWE-835's infinite loop with unreachable exit. This is distinct from an out-of-bounds read, since the missing constraint is loop termination, not memory access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the inner decode loop's only exit depends on encountering DW_LNE_end_sequence, and the loop condition does not check line_ptr against line_end. A crafted ELF whose line table omits that opcode keeps `end_sequence` false while standard opcodes continue to be decoded, so the loop never terminates, consuming CPU (DoS).

commit_msg:
As part of CVE-2013-4288, the D-Bus clients were allowed (and
encouraged) to submit the UID of the subject of authorization checks
to avoid races against UID changes (notably using executables
set-UID to root).

However, that also allowed any client to submit an arbitrary UID, and
that could be used to bypass "can only ask about / affect the same UID"
checks in CheckAuthorization / RegisterAuthenticationAgent /
UnregisterAuthenticationAgent.  This allowed an attacker:

- With CheckAuthorization, to cause the registered authentication
  agent in victim's session to pop up a dialog, or to determine whether
  the victim currently has a temporary authorization to perform an
  operation.

  (In principle, the attacker can also determine whether JavaScript
  rules allow the victim process to perform an operation; however,
  usually rules base their decisions on information determined from
  the supplied UID, so the attacker usually won't learn anything new.)

- With RegisterAuthenticationAgent, to prevent the victim's
  authentication agent to work (for a specific victim process),
  or to learn about which operations requiring authorization
  the victim is attempting.

To fix this, expose internal _polkit_unix_process_get_owner() /
obsolete polkit_unix_process_get_owner() as a private
polkit_unix_process_get_racy_uid__() (being more explicit about the
dangers on relying on it), and use it in
polkit_backend_session_monitor_get_user_for_subject() to return
a boolean indicating whether the subject UID may be caller-chosen.

Then, in the permission checks that require the subject to be
equal to the caller, fail on caller-chosen UIDs (and continue
through the pre-existing code paths which allow root, or root-designated
server processes, to ask about arbitrary subjects.)

Signed-off-by: Miloslav Trmač <mitr@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                                                                        caller,', '                                                                         subject,', "   *    if details are passed (otherwise you'd be able to spoof the dialog)", '  if (!polkit_identity_equal (user_of_caller, user_of_subject) || has_details)'], 'added_lines': ['  gboolean user_of_subject_matches;', '                                                                        caller, NULL,', '                                                                         subject, &user_of_subject_matches,', "   *    if details are passed (otherwise you'd be able to spoof the dialog);", '   *    the caller supplies the user_of_subject value, so we additionally', '   *    require it to match at least at one point in time (via', '   *    user_of_subject_matches).', '  if (!user_of_subject_matches', '      || !polkit_identity_equal (user_of_caller, user_of_subject)', '      || has_details)']}
description: A flaw was found in polkit before version 0.116. The implementation of the polkit_backend_interactive_authority_check_authorization function in polkitd allows to test for authentication and trigger authentication of unrelated processes owned by other users. This may result in a local DoS and information disclosure.

code_evidence: The subject's user identity is resolved from caller-supplied subject data via polkit_backend_session_monitor_get_user_for_subject; the return value only yields user_of_subject, with no indication that the UID was caller-chosen.

The authorization gate compares user_of_caller against user_of_subject and only rejects when identities differ or details are present; a caller can supply a subject whose reported UID equals the caller's, so the same-user restriction is satisfied with an attacker-chosen value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a same-user authorization check that can be satisfied with attacker-controlled input, so the intended access-control constraint is effectively absent for crafted subjects. This is missing/ineffective authorization (CWE-862), not merely an input-validation bug, because the security decision rests on an unverified subject attribute.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the backend trusts the subject-provided UID without verifying it was not caller-chosen. Trigger: a client submits a crafted subject whose resolved UID matches its own. Consequence: CheckAuthorization proceeds for unrelated processes/identities owned by other users, enabling authentication-dialog triggering, authorization-state probing, and doS/information disclosure.

commit_msg:
dm: fix race between dm_get_from_kobject() and __dm_destroy()

The following BUG_ON was hit when testing repeat creation and removal of
DM devices:

    kernel BUG at drivers/md/dm.c:2919!
    CPU: 7 PID: 750 Comm: systemd-udevd Not tainted 4.1.44
    Call Trace:
     [<ffffffff81649e8b>] dm_get_from_kobject+0x34/0x3a
     [<ffffffff81650ef1>] dm_attr_show+0x2b/0x5e
     [<ffffffff817b46d1>] ? mutex_lock+0x26/0x44
     [<ffffffff811df7f5>] sysfs_kf_seq_show+0x83/0xcf
     [<ffffffff811de257>] kernfs_seq_show+0x23/0x25
     [<ffffffff81199118>] seq_read+0x16f/0x325
     [<ffffffff811de994>] kernfs_fop_read+0x3a/0x13f
     [<ffffffff8117b625>] __vfs_read+0x26/0x9d
     [<ffffffff8130eb59>] ? security_file_permission+0x3c/0x44
     [<ffffffff8117bdb8>] ? rw_verify_area+0x83/0xd9
     [<ffffffff8117be9d>] vfs_read+0x8f/0xcf
     [<ffffffff81193e34>] ? __fdget_pos+0x12/0x41
     [<ffffffff8117c686>] SyS_read+0x4b/0x76
     [<ffffffff817b606e>] system_call_fastpath+0x12/0x71

The bug can be easily triggered, if an extra delay (e.g. 10ms) is added
between the test of DMF_FREEING & DMF_DELETING and dm_get() in
dm_get_from_kobject().

To fix it, we need to ensure the test of DMF_FREEING & DMF_DELETING and
dm_get() are done in an atomic way, so _minor_lock is used.

The other callers of dm_get() have also been checked to be OK: some
callers invoke dm_get() under _minor_lock, some callers invoke it under
_hash_lock, and dm_start_request() invoke it after increasing
md->open_count.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Hou Tao <houtao1@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Mike Snitzer <snitzer@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (test_bit(DMF_FREEING, &md->flags) ||', '\t    dm_deleting_md(md))', '\t\treturn NULL;', '\tdm_get(md);'], 'added_lines': ['\tspin_lock(&_minor_lock);', '\tif (test_bit(DMF_FREEING, &md->flags) || dm_deleting_md(md)) {', '\t\tmd = NULL;', '\t\tgoto out;', '\t}', '\tdm_get(md);', 'out:', '\tspin_unlock(&_minor_lock);']}
description: The dm_get_from_kobject function in drivers/md/dm.c in the Linux kernel before 4.14.3 allow local users to cause a denial of service (BUG) by leveraging a race condition with __dm_destroy during creation and removal of DM devices.

code_evidence: The function tests DMF_FREEING and dm_deleting_md(md) on the shared md->flags state, then separately calls dm_get(md) without holding _minor_lock. Because the check and the reference acquisition are not atomic, __dm_destroy can transition the device to freeing/deleting and tear it down between the test and dm_get().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because a shared resource (the mapped_device and its flags) is accessed through a non-atomic check-then-act sequence, allowing a concurrent interfering code sequence to modify that resource. This is improper synchronization, not merely a missing NULL check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the DMF_FREEING/DMF_DELETING check and dm_get() reference acquisition are performed without mutual exclusion against __dm_destroy. Trigger: concurrent creation/removal of DM devices causes __dm_destroy to run in the window between the check and dm_get(). Consequence: dm_get() operates on a device being destroyed, leading to the observed BUG/denial of service.

commit_msg: Prevent HTTP pipelining which Crow doesn't support.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['                parser_.clear();']}
description: HTTP applications (servers) based on Crow through 1.0+4 may allow a Use-After-Free and code execution when HTTP pipelining is used. The HTTP parser supports HTTP pipelining, but the asynchronous Connection layer is unaware of HTTP pipelining. Specifically, the Connection layer is unaware that it has begun processing a later request before it has finished processing an earlier request.

code_evidence: After the response is written, res.end(), res.clear() and buffers_.clear() release the response state, but the parser state (parser_) is not reset here; the added parser_.clear() in the patch indicates the parser previously retained state across requests.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The described consequence is reuse of freed memory (res/buffers_ state) because parser and connection layers disagree on request boundaries, matching CWE-416 Use After Free. It is not merely a parsing/logic error, since the supported impact is memory reuse after free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the connection layer finishes and clears response buffers without resetting the HTTP parser, so pipelined bytes for a later request are parsed while the earlier request is still being processed. Trigger: a client sends pipelined requests; the parser advances into the next request prematurely, and the connection layer later frees/reuses objects (res, buffers_) still referenced by the in-flight handling, yielding a use-after-free and possible code execution.

commit_msg:
objstack: assert that the alloc size will fit within a chunk
to prevent a buffer overflow

Bug found using OSS-Fuze.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (bottom > top) {new_chunk(); tmp = bottom; bottom += size;}'], 'added_lines': ['    if (bottom > top) {check_size(size); new_chunk(); tmp = bottom; bottom += size;}']}
description: objstack in GNU Aspell 0.60.8 has a heap-based buffer overflow in acommon::ObjStack::dup_top (called from acommon::StringMap::add and acommon::Config::lookup_list).

code_evidence: Line 3 advances bottom by size without checking that the allocation fits within the current chunk. Line 4 only calls new_chunk() when bottom > top; the size check on the new chunk is absent, so a requested size larger than the chunk capacity leaves bottom beyond top after the second bottom += size, and the returned tmp pointer (line 2/4) is used by callers to write size bytes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the missing size constraint allows the returned allocation pointer to reference memory beyond the intended buffer, and callers write past its end. This is a direct out-of-bounds write caused by an unchecked allocation size, not merely an integer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: alloc_bottom advances the bottom pointer and returns a buffer without verifying that size fits within the chunk capacity (line 4 only checks overflow condition, not size vs. chunk). Trigger: a caller requests a size exceeding the newly allocated chunk. Consequence: subsequent writes through the returned pointer go past the chunk end, a heap-based out-of-bounds write.

It's not necessary to unregister pin controller device registered
with devm_pinctrl_register() and using pinctrl_unregister() leads
to a double free.

Signed-off-by: Linus Walleij <linus.walleij@linaro.org>

code_evidence: amd_gpio_remove obtains gpio_dev from platform_get_drvdata, removes the gpiochip, then unconditionally calls pinctrl_unregister(gpio_dev->pctrl). The device was registered with devm_pinctrl_register(), so the pin controller is already subject to devres-managed cleanup; the explicit unregister in the remove path frees the same pinctrl object a second time.

commit_msg:
Fix vulnerability in enc_untrusted_recvfrom

Change recvfrom memcpy to check for received_buffer size to avoid
copying extra buffer.

This issue was reported by Qinkun Bao, Zhaofeng Chen, Mingshen Sun, and
Kang Li from Baidu Security.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 322476299
Change-Id: I3606ff9ec51ec7cc4312c7555c645a2fc6e09b21
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  memcpy(buf, buffer_received.data(), len);'], 'added_lines': ['  memcpy(buf, buffer_received.data(), std::min(len, buffer_received.size()));']}
description: A buffer length validation vulnerability in Asylo versions prior to 0.6.0 allows an attacker to read data they should not have access to. The 'enc_untrusted_recvfrom' function generates a return value which is deserialized by 'MessageReader', and copied into three different 'extents'. The length of the third 'extents' is controlled by the outside world, and not verified on copy, allowing the attacker to force Asylo to copy trusted memory data into an untrusted buffer of significantly small length.. We recommend updating Asylo to version 0.6.0 or later.

code_evidence: Line 10 places the caller-supplied len into the request; line 22 extracts the deserialized response buffer via output.next() without obtaining or validating its size; line 23 then calls memcpy(buf, buffer_received.data(), len), copying len bytes regardless of how many bytes buffer_received actually holds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because memcpy copies an input buffer to an output buffer without checking that the input size is sufficient/consistent with the copy length, the classic unchecked buffer-copy pattern. The observed consequence is an out-of-bounds read, which the CWE notes may map toward CWE-125, but the unchecked-size copy root cause here matches CWE-120.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the unchecked copy length: memcpy uses the caller/request len rather than the size of the received buffer. If the deserialized buffer is shorter than len, the copy reads past the source buffer's end, leaking trusted memory into the caller's buf; the consequence is an out-of-bounds read (information disclosure), not a write overflow.

Aside from being a nice cleanup, these will to allow the upcoming direct

Signed-off-by: Ben Skeggs <bskeggs@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (vma->addr != addr) {', '\t\t\tconst u64 tail = vma->size + vma->addr - addr;', '\t\t\tif (ret = -ENOMEM, !(vma = nvkm_vma_tail(vma, tail)))', '\t\t\t\tgoto fail;', '\t\t\tvma->part = true;', '\t\t\tnvkm_vmm_node_insert(vmm, vma);', '\t\t}', '', '\t\tif (vma->size != size) {', '\t\t\tconst u64 tail = vma->size - size;', '\t\t\tstruct nvkm_vma *tmp;', '\t\t\tif (ret = -ENOMEM, !(tmp = nvkm_vma_tail(vma, tail))) {', '\t\t\t\tnvkm_vmm_unmap_region(vmm, vma);', '\t\t\t\tgoto fail;', '\t\t\t}', '\t\t\ttmp->part = true;', '\t\t\tnvkm_vmm_node_insert(vmm, tmp);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tvma = nvkm_vmm_node_split(vmm, vma, addr, size);', '\t\tif (!vma) {', '\t\t\tret = -ENOMEM;', '\t\t\tgoto fail;']}
description: A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s nouveau driver in how a user triggers a memory overflow that causes the nvkm_vma_tail function to fail. This flaw allows a local user to crash or potentially escalate their privileges on the system.

code_evidence: When vma->addr != addr, the code computes tail = vma->size + vma->addr - addr and reassigns vma = nvkm_vma_tail(vma, tail); the original node is consumed and a new node returned, then inserted.
When vma->size != size, tail = vma->size - size is computed and nvkm_vma_tail(vma, tail) is called; on failure the code calls nvkm_vmm_unmap_region(vmm, vma) and jumps to fail, still referencing vma.
At line 71 the fail/error path calls nvkm_vmm_unmap_region(vmm, vma) after the split logic may have already freed or unmapped the original vma, so vma is used after its backing node was released.

vma->busy = false;
nvkm_vmm_unmap_region(vmm, vma);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The split logic frees/replaces the original vma via nvkm_vma_tail but the error path (and line 71) continues to reference the original vma pointer. Triggering the size-split failure or a later map failure causes nvkm_vmm_unmap_region to operate on freed memory, leading to a use-after-free that can crash or corrupt kernel memory.
