commit_msg:
ICO: fix integer overflow

#50
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (entries.back().dwImageOffset + entries.back().dwBytesInRes > size_) {'], 'added_lines': ['  if (static_cast<uint64_t>(entries.back().dwImageOffset) + entries.back().dwBytesInRes > size_) {']}
description: Leanify 0.4.3 allows remote attackers to trigger an out-of-bounds write (1024 bytes) via a modified input file.

code_evidence: The bounds check compares entries.back().dwImageOffset + entries.back().dwBytesInRes against size_ using 32-bit uint32_t arithmetic; the sum can wrap before the comparison, letting the check pass for an oversized offset.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The wrapped check permits an out-of-range destination offset that is then used as a write location, directly producing an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The integer overflow is the cause; the OOB write is the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: 32-bit addition overflow in the offset+size bounds check at line 16. Trigger: a modified ICO file whose last entry has a large dwImageOffset so the sum wraps below size_. Consequence: the check is bypassed, and later memmove/memcpy at lines 51/57 writes to fp_ + dwImageOffset - size_leanified outside the buffer, an out-of-bounds write.

commit_msg:
ax25: Fix NULL pointer dereferences in ax25 timers

The previous commit 7ec02f5ac8a5 ("ax25: fix NPD bug in ax25_disconnect")
move ax25_disconnect into lock_sock() in order to prevent NPD bugs. But
there are race conditions that may lead to null pointer dereferences in
ax25_heartbeat_expiry(), ax25_t1timer_expiry(), ax25_t2timer_expiry(),
ax25_t3timer_expiry() and ax25_idletimer_expiry(), when we use
ax25_kill_by_device() to detach the ax25 device.

One of the race conditions that cause null pointer dereferences can be
shown as below:

      (Thread 1)                    |      (Thread 2)
ax25_connect()                      |
 ax25_std_establish_data_link()     |
  ax25_start_t1timer()              |
   mod_timer(&ax25->t1timer,..)     |
                                    | ax25_kill_by_device()
   (wait a time)                    |  ...
                                    |  s->ax25_dev = NULL; //(1)
   ax25_t1timer_expiry()            |
    ax25->ax25_dev->values[..] //(2)|  ...
     ...                            |

We set null to ax25_cb->ax25_dev in position (1) and dereference
the null pointer in position (2).

The corresponding fail log is shown below:
===============================================================
BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000050
CPU: 1 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/1 Not tainted 5.17.0-rc6-00794-g45690b7d0
RIP: 0010:ax25_t1timer_expiry+0x12/0x40
...
Call Trace:
 call_timer_fn+0x21/0x120
 __run_timers.part.0+0x1ca/0x250
 run_timer_softirq+0x2c/0x60
 __do_softirq+0xef/0x2f3
 irq_exit_rcu+0xb6/0x100
 sysvec_apic_timer_interrupt+0xa2/0xd0
...

This patch moves ax25_disconnect() before s->ax25_dev = NULL
and uses del_timer_sync() to delete timers in ax25_disconnect().
If ax25_disconnect() is called by ax25_kill_by_device() or
ax25->ax25_dev is NULL, the reason in ax25_disconnect() will be
equal to ENETUNREACH, it will wait all timers to stop before we
set null to s->ax25_dev in ax25_kill_by_device().

Fixes: 7ec02f5ac8a5 ("ax25: fix NPD bug in ax25_disconnect")
Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

description: A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s Amateur Radio AX.25 protocol functionality in the way a user connects with the protocol. This flaw allows a local user to crash the system.

code_evidence: Lines 4-9 stop timers with non-synchronous ax25_stop_* helpers unless ax25->sk is NULL or marked SOCK_DESTROY; an expiry callback may still be running and dereference ax25->ax25_dev after ax25_kill_by_device() sets it to NULL.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw is a dereference of a pointer (ax25->ax25_dev) expected to be valid but set to NULL by a racing detach, matching CWE-476. The socket accesses in this function are NULL-checked, so a use-after-free or race weakness label would not fit the observed dereference as precisely.

Trigger: a timer fires after the device detach. Consequence: NULL dereference in the expiry callback, causing a kernel crash (availability impact).

commit_msg:
crypto: algif_hash - Only export and import on sockets with data

The hash_accept call fails to work on sockets that have not received
any data.  For some algorithm implementations it may cause crashes.

This patch fixes this by ensuring that we only export and import on
sockets that have received data.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: Harsh Jain <harshjain.prof@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>
Tested-by: Stephan Mueller <smueller@chronox.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\terr = crypto_ahash_export(req, state);', '\tctx2->more = 1;'], 'added_lines': ['\tbool more;', '\tlock_sock(sk);', '\tmore = ctx->more;', '\terr = more ? crypto_ahash_export(req, state) : 0;', '\trelease_sock(sk);', '', '\tctx2->more = more;', '', '\tif (!more)', '\t\treturn err;']}
description: The hash_accept function in crypto/algif_hash.c in the Linux kernel before 4.3.6 allows local users to cause a denial of service (OOPS) by attempting to trigger use of in-kernel hash algorithms for a socket that has received zero bytes of data.

code_evidence: hash_accept unconditionally calls crypto_ahash_export(req, state) on the socket's request without checking whether the socket has received any data (ctx->more).
It then unconditionally sets ctx2->more = 1 and calls crypto_ahash_import(&ctx2->req, state), assuming the exported state is valid even when nothing was received.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the unchecked zero-data path drives crypto_ahash_export/import on a request whose internal state pointers may be NULL, causing a NULL dereference and OOPS. The fix guards these calls with the ctx->more data-present flag, confirming the missing precondition is the root cause rather than a generic logic error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the accept path assumes the hash request holds an initialized/exportable state and that ctx->more is set. Trigger: a local user calls accept on an AF_ALG hash socket that has received zero bytes. Export/import on an uninitialized request can dereference internal pointers that are NULL, producing an OOPS/DoS. Consequence is a kernel crash (availability), not memory corruption directly evidenced here.

commit_msg: Fix strncat/cpy bounding issues (fix #1425)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (isnan(val)) strncpy(str,"NaN",len);', '    if (val<0) strncpy(str,"-Infinity",len);', '    else strncpy(str,"Infinity",len);'], 'added_lines': ['  assert(len>9); // in case if strcpy', '  if (isnan(val)) strcpy(str,"NaN");', '    if (val<0) strcpy(str,"-Infinity");', '    else strcpy(str,"Infinity");']}
description: Espruino before 1.99 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) and a potential Escalation of Privileges with a user crafted input file via a Buffer Overflow during syntax parsing, because strncat is misused.

code_evidence: The function copies fixed string literals into the caller-supplied buffer str using strncpy(str, "NaN", len), strncpy(str, "-Infinity", len), and strncpy(str, "Infinity", len). The only bound is len, which is not validated before these calls; if the caller passes a len larger than the actual destination buffer capacity, strncpy writes up to len bytes (including the literal plus NUL padding) past the buffer's intended boundary. The non-finite branches therefore perform unbounded-in-practice writes controlled by the len argument.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes to a memory buffer without a constraint tying len to the buffer's actual capacity, producing an out-of-bounds write, which is the direct concern of CWE-119. This is a buffer-bounds failure rather than an integer or format-string flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the copy length len is trusted without confirming it is within the destination buffer's real size. Trigger: a crafted input path that reaches ftoa_bounded_extra with a NaN or Infinity value and an oversized len. Consequence: a write beyond the buffer, corrupting adjacent memory and potentially crashing or enabling escalation.

commit_msg:
[Fix] libmodplug: C API: Limit the length of strings copied to the output buffer of ModPlug_InstrumentName() and ModPlug_SampleName() to 32 bytes (including terminating null) as is done by original libmodplug. This avoids potential buffer overflows in software relying on this limit instead of querying the required buffer size beforehand. libopenmpt can return strings longer than 32 bytes here beacuse the internal limit of 32 bytes applies to strings encoded in arbitrary character encodings but the API returns them converted to UTF-8, which can be longer. (reported by Antonio Morales Maldonado of Semmle Security Research Team)

git-svn-id: https://source.openmpt.org/svn/openmpt/trunk/OpenMPT@12127 56274372-70c3-4bfc-bfc3-4c3a0b034d27
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tunsigned int retval;', '\tsize_t tmpretval;', '\tif(!str){', '\t\tif(buff){', "\t\t\t*buff = '\\0';", '\t\t}', '\t\treturn 0;', '\ttmpretval = strlen(str);', '\tif(tmpretval>=INT_MAX){', '\t\ttmpretval = INT_MAX-1;', '\tretval = (int)tmpretval;', '\tif(buff){', '\t\tmemcpy(buff,str,retval+1);', "\t\tbuff[retval] = '\\0';", '\t}', '\topenmpt_free_string(str);', '\treturn retval;'], 'added_lines': ['\tchar buf[32];', '\tmemset(buf,0,32);', '\tif(str){', '\t\tstrncpy(buf,str,31);', '\t\topenmpt_free_string(str);', '\tif(buff){', '\t\tstrncpy(buff,buf,32);', '\treturn (unsigned int)strlen(buf);']}
description: In libopenmpt before 0.3.19 and 0.4.x before 0.4.9, ModPlug_InstrumentName and ModPlug_SampleName in libopenmpt_modplug.c do not restrict the lengths of libmodplug output-buffer strings in the C API, leading to a buffer overflow.

code_evidence: Line 7 obtains an instrument name string of arbitrary length from openmpt_module_get_instrument_name. Line 14 computes its length with strlen, and lines 18-21 copy retval+1 bytes into the caller-supplied buff via memcpy without any knowledge of buff's allocated size; the only bound is INT_MAX, which does not reflect the destination capacity.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because an input buffer is copied to an output buffer without verifying the input size is less than the output size; the unchecked memcpy of retval+1 bytes is the classic buffer-copy overflow, distinct from an out-of-bounds read or integer-size miscalculation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function copies the full source string plus terminator into the caller's output buffer using memcpy sized by strlen(str), never checking the destination size. Trigger: a caller passing a buff smaller than the returned name (the libmodplug API contract assumes 32 bytes). Consequence: heap/stack overflow, memory corruption and possible code execution or crash.

commit_msg: fix #164: Integer overflow related to reg->dmax in search_in_range()
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        sch_range = (UChar* )range + reg->dist_max;', '        if (sch_range > end) sch_range = (UChar* )end;'], 'added_lines': ['        if ((ptrdiff_t )(end - range) > (ptrdiff_t )reg->dist_max)', '          sch_range = (UChar* )range + reg->dist_max;', '        else', '          sch_range = (UChar* )end;']}
description: An integer overflow in the search_in_range function in regexec.c in Oniguruma 6.x before 6.9.4_rc2 leads to an out-of-bounds read, in which the offset of this read is under the control of an attacker. (This only affects the 32-bit compiled version). Remote attackers can cause a denial-of-service or information disclosure, or possibly have unspecified other impact, via a crafted regular expression.

code_evidence: The code computes sch_range = range + reg->dist_max without first bounding reg->dist_max against end - range. On a 32-bit build, if dist_max is large relative to the remaining buffer, the pointer addition wraps, so the subsequent sch_range > end clamp compares against a wrapped (small) pointer and fails to clamp.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the arithmetic on reg->dist_max and the pointer offset overflows/wraps before the bound check, and the logic assumes the sum stays larger than range. The patch converts to ptrdiff_t comparison to prevent the wrap; this is integer overflow, not merely an off-by-one bounds-check flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is an unchecked pointer/integer addition range + reg->dist_max that can wrap on 32-bit. Trigger is an attacker-influenced regex producing a large dist_max with a short remaining range. The wrapped sch_range is passed to forward_search as the search bound, enabling out-of-bounds reads (DoS/info disclosure).

Problem:    Reading past end of completion with duplicate match.
Solution:   Check string length

commit_msg: Add addition overflow check for stream buffer (#226)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        xBufferSizeBytes++;', '        pucAllocatedMemory = ( uint8_t * ) pvPortMalloc( xBufferSizeBytes + sizeof( StreamBuffer_t ) ); /*lint !e9079 malloc() only returns void*. */'], 'added_lines': ['        if( xBufferSizeBytes < ( xBufferSizeBytes + 1 + sizeof( StreamBuffer_t ) ) )', '        {', '            xBufferSizeBytes++;', '            pucAllocatedMemory = ( uint8_t * ) pvPortMalloc( xBufferSizeBytes + sizeof( StreamBuffer_t ) ); /*lint !e9079 malloc() only returns void*. */', '        }', '        else', '        {', '            pucAllocatedMemory = NULL;', '        }', '        ']}
description: The kernel in Amazon Web Services FreeRTOS before 10.4.3 has an integer overflow in stream_buffer.c for a stream buffer.

code_evidence: xBufferSizeBytes (size_t, caller-controlled) is incremented at line 22, then xBufferSizeBytes + sizeof(StreamBuffer_t) is computed and passed as the malloc size at line 23. No check constrains xBufferSizeBytes near SIZE_MAX before these arithmetic operations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because a size_t increment and addition used for allocation size can overflow/wrap, and the code does not validate the result against the original value. This is integer overflow feeding a memory-allocation size, not a mere out-of-bounds read/write variant.

evidence_lines.code:
xBufferSizeBytes++;
pucAllocatedMemory = ( uint8_t * ) pvPortMalloc( xBufferSizeBytes + sizeof( StreamBuffer_t ) );

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size arithmetic xBufferSizeBytes++ and xBufferSizeBytes + sizeof(StreamBuffer_t) can wrap when xBufferSizeBytes is near SIZE_MAX. Trigger: a caller supplies a very large buffer size. Consequence: pvPortMalloc receives a small/wrapped allocation size, so a smaller block than the logical buffer is returned, and prvInitialiseNewStreamBuffer then treats it as xBufferSizeBytes, enabling out-of-bounds writes and heap corruption.

commit_msg:
disable UDP port by default

As reported, UDP amplification attacks have started to use insecure
internet-exposed memcached instances. UDP used to be a lot more popular as a
transport for memcached many years ago, but I'm not aware of many recent
users.

Ten years ago, the TCP connection overhead from many clients was relatively
high (dozens or hundreds per client server), but these days many clients are
batched, or user fewer processes, or simply anre't worried about it.

While changing the default to listen on localhost only would also help, the
true culprit is UDP. There are many more use cases for using memcached over
the network than there are for using the UDP protocol.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    settings.udpport = 11211;'], 'added_lines': ['    settings.udpport = 0;']}
description: Memcached version 1.5.5 contains an Insufficient Control of Network Message Volume (Network Amplification, CWE-406) vulnerability in the UDP support of the memcached server that can result in denial of service via network flood (traffic amplification of 1:50,000 has been reported by reliable sources). This attack appear to be exploitable via network connectivity to port 11211 UDP. This vulnerability appears to have been fixed in 1.5.6 due to the disabling of the UDP protocol by default.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: settings_init only assigns default configuration values; the UDP port default itself is not an operation that allocates or maintains a limited resource, so the function does not directly demonstrate uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-400).

commit_msg:
CVE-2016-0798: avoid memory leak in SRP

The SRP user database lookup method SRP_VBASE_get_by_user had confusing
memory management semantics; the returned pointer was sometimes newly
allocated, and sometimes owned by the callee. The calling code has no
way of distinguishing these two cases.

Specifically, SRP servers that configure a secret seed to hide valid
login information are vulnerable to a memory leak: an attacker
connecting with an invalid username can cause a memory leak of around
300 bytes per connection.

Servers that do not configure SRP, or configure SRP but do not configure
a seed are not vulnerable.

In Apache, the seed directive is known as SSLSRPUnknownUserSeed.

To mitigate the memory leak, the seed handling in SRP_VBASE_get_by_user
is now disabled even if the user has configured a seed.

Applications are advised to migrate to SRP_VBASE_get1_by_user. However,
note that OpenSSL makes no strong guarantees about the
indistinguishability of valid and invalid logins. In particular,
computations are currently not carried out in constant time.

Reviewed-by: Rich Salz <rsalz@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                SRP_VBASE_get_by_user(srp_callback_parm.vb,', '                                      srp_callback_parm.login);', '                        SRP_VBASE_get_by_user(srp_callback_parm.vb,', '                                              srp_callback_parm.login);'], 'added_lines': ['            SRP_user_pwd_free(srp_callback_parm.user);', '                SRP_VBASE_get1_by_user(srp_callback_parm.vb,', '                                       srp_callback_parm.login);', '                    SRP_user_pwd_free(srp_callback_parm.user);', '                        SRP_VBASE_get1_by_user(srp_callback_parm.vb,', '                                               srp_callback_parm.login);']}
description: Memory leak in the SRP_VBASE_get_by_user implementation in OpenSSL 1.0.1 before 1.0.1s and 1.0.2 before 1.0.2g allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by providing an invalid username in a connection attempt, related to apps/s_server.c and crypto/srp/srp_vfy.c.

code_evidence: On a special BIO retry during handshake, the function calls SRP_VBASE_get_by_user and overwrites srp_callback_parm.user without freeing any previously stored pointer, then continues the loop.
The same overwrite occurs on the read path: the lookup result is reassigned to srp_callback_parm.user and the loop continues, so each repeated lookup can orphan the prior allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function mismanages an allocated SRP user structure across repeated lookups, causing unbounded resource consumption, which aligns with the resource-management category CWE-399; the concrete effect is a memory leak leading to DoS rather than a separate weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of SRP_VBASE_get_by_user has ambiguous ownership (sometimes newly allocated, sometimes callee-owned) and is stored in srp_callback_parm.user without freeing the previous value. Trigger: a remote client whose handshake repeatedly returns BIO_RR_SSL_X509_LOOKUP (e.g. invalid username with a configured seed) causes repeated lookups. Consequence: leaked allocations accumulate per connection, enabling memory exhaustion and denial of service.

Decoder: Set u1_long_term_reference_flag to 0 for error concealment

For MBs which are in error, set u1_long_term_reference_flag to zero.
This ensures latest frame is used for concealment

Bug: 28470138
Change-Id: I58eab5bc1da277823f3dbb4103ba50867f8935dc
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [''], 'added_lines': ['    ps_dec->ps_dpb_cmds->u1_long_term_reference_flag = 0;']}
description: decoder/ih264d_parse_pslice.c in mediaserver in Android 6.x before 2016-07-01 does not properly select concealment frames, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (device hang or reboot) via a crafted media file, aka internal bug 28470138.

code_evidence: The function handles error concealment: when REJECT_CUR_PIC is set it aborts, otherwise it branches on prev_slice_err. For the first-slice error case it rebuilds slice state and calls ih264d_start_of_pic, whose return value is checked.

In the prev_slice_err==1 path the slice/DPB state is set up and start_of_pic is invoked; the function relies on the decoder's DPB command state (u1_long_term_reference_flag) established elsewhere, and the diff adds a reset of that flag before this branch.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function processes untrusted bitstream-derived state without validating the long-term reference flag before using it for concealment, matching improper validation of input properties (CWE-20). The consequence is availability loss, consistent with the target weakness's DoS scope.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that error-concealment state derived from a crafted media file is not constrained: the long-term reference flag in the DPB command structure is left at an attacker-influenced value, so concealment selects the wrong (long-term) reference frame. Triggering a corrupted P-slice error path with such a flag yields incorrect concealment frame selection, supporting a device hang or reboot.

description:
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux Kernel io_uring system can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

The io_file_get_fixed function lacks the presence of ctx->uring_lock which can lead to a Use-After-Free vulnerability due a race condition with fixed files getting unregistered.

We recommend upgrading past commit da24142b1ef9fd5d36b76e36bab328a5b27523e8.

code_evidence: Line 3 declares __must_hold(&ctx->uring_lock), so io_init_req always runs with uring_lock held. Line 40-41 call io_file_get with a literal 0 flags argument for fixed-file lookups instead of IO_URING_F_NONBLOCK, so the callee cannot know the lock is already held and may take it again or use an unlocked path while fixed files are concurrently unregistered.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing lock indicator allows a fixed-file pointer to be used after its backing resource is freed by concurrent unregistration, which is a use-after-free (CWE-416). It is a race-driven lifetime bug, not merely an access-control issue, so CWE-416 fits the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the flags argument 0 fails to signal to io_file_get/io_file_get_fixed that ctx->uring_lock is held, so the fixed-file lookup races with fixed-file unregistration. Trigger: submit a request with IOSQE_FIXED_FILE while another thread unregisters the fixed file table. Consequence: the file reference is obtained without proper serialization, enabling use-after-free and potential local privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
Jan Kara's analysis of the syzbot report (edited):

  The reproducer opens a directory on FUSE filesystem, it then attaches
  dnotify mark to the open directory.  After that a fuse_do_getattr() call
  finds that attributes returned by the server are inconsistent, and calls
  make_bad_inode() which, among other things does:

          inode->i_mode = S_IFREG;

  This then confuses dnotify which doesn't tear down its structures
  properly and eventually crashes.

Avoid calling make_bad_inode() on a live inode: switch to a private flag on
the fuse inode.  Also add the test to ops which the bad_inode_ops would
have caught.

This bug goes back to the initial merge of fuse in 2.6.14...

Reported-by: syzbot+f427adf9324b92652ccc@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>
Tested-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (fuse_is_bad(inode))', '\t\treturn -EIO;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the FUSE filesystem implementation in the Linux kernel before 5.10.6, aka CID-5d069dbe8aaf. fuse_do_getattr() calls make_bad_inode() in inappropriate situations, causing a system crash. NOTE: the original fix for this vulnerability was incomplete, and its incompleteness is tracked as CVE-2021-28950.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function is fuse_permission, which only performs permission checks; the added fuse_is_bad guard is a defensive check, and the function contains no resource allocation, cleanup, or make_bad_inode call, so it does not directly demonstrate incomplete cleanup (CWE-459).

commit_msg:
usb:xhci:fix memory leak in usb_xhci_exit

If the xhci uses msix, it doesn't free the corresponding
memory, thus leading a memory leak. This patch avoid this.

Signed-off-by: Li Qiang <liqiang6-s@360.cn>
Message-id: 57d7d2e0.d4301c0a.d13e9.9a55@mx.google.com
Signed-off-by: Gerd Hoffmann <kraxel@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        memory_region_del_subregion(&xhci->mem, &dev->msix_table_mmio);', '        memory_region_del_subregion(&xhci->mem, &dev->msix_pba_mmio);'], 'added_lines': ['        msix_uninit(dev, &xhci->mem, &xhci->mem);']}
description: Memory leak in the usb_xhci_exit function in hw/usb/hcd-xhci.c in QEMU (aka Quick Emulator), when the xhci uses msix, allows local guest OS administrators to cause a denial of service (memory consumption and possibly QEMU process crash) by repeatedly unplugging a USB device.

code_evidence: On the msix path (dev->msix_table, dev->msix_pba, dev->msix_entry_used all set), exit only removes the msix_table_mmio and msix_pba_mmio subregions from xhci->mem; it does not call msix_uninit to free the msix objects allocated when msix was initialized.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-772 fits because the function ends the device lifetime without releasing the msix resource allocated during initialization; the missing release is the weakness, and resource exhaustion is the consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the msix teardown path removes MMIO subregions but omits msix_uninit, so msix-related allocations are never freed. Trigger: repeatedly unplugging a USB device whose xhci uses msix runs this exit path each time, accumulating unfreed memory and eventually causing DoS via memory consumption or QEMU process crash.

commit_msg:
Disallow negative ngram_widths values in tf.raw_ops.StringNGrams

PiperOrigin-RevId: 387148179
Change-Id: I641395a09a208be72ef9b3ceb128cf8a83a0775b
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    for (int ngram_width : ngram_widths_) {', '      OP_REQUIRES(', '          context, ngram_width > 0,', '          errors::InvalidArgument("ngram_widths must contain positive values"));', '    }', '']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions the implementation of `tf.raw_ops.StringNGrams` is vulnerable to an integer overflow issue caused by converting a signed integer value to an unsigned one and then allocating memory based on this value. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/8d72537c6abf5a44103b57b9c2e22c14f5f49698/tensorflow/core/kernels/string_ngrams_op.cc#L184) calls `reserve` on a `tstring` with a value that sometimes can be negative if user supplies negative `ngram_widths`. The `reserve` method calls `TF_TString_Reserve` which has an `unsigned long` argument for the size of the buffer. Hence, the implicit conversion transforms the negative value to a large integer. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit c283e542a3f422420cfdb332414543b62fc4e4a5. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: The loop at lines 47-48 iterates over ngram_widths_ and accumulates get_num_ngrams(length, ngram_width) into num_ngrams without validating that ngram_width is positive; a negative width flows into the arithmetic.

At lines 63-68 each ngram_width is again passed to get_num_ngrams and CreateNgrams, and num_ngrams is added to output_start_idx, propagating the negative-derived count into output sizing and pointer arithmetic.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The signed negative width is implicitly converted to an unsigned size when used for allocation/reserve, matching CWE-681 (incorrect conversion between numeric types). The patch's added ngram_width > 0 guard confirms the missing constraint; the defect is the signed-to-unsigned conversion, not merely an out-of-range index.

evidence_lines.code:
for (int ngram_width : ngram_widths_)
num_ngrams += get_num_ngrams(length, ngram_width);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: ngram_widths_ values are used in arithmetic without a positivity check, so a negative width yields a negative num_ngrams. This negative count then feeds output tensor allocation and CreateNgrams, where it is converted to unsigned buffer sizes, producing an oversized allocation or out-of-bounds access.

commit_msg:
Currently, we have a bug where a simultaneous DROPTAG ioctl and socket
close may race, as we attempt to remove a key from lists twice, and
perform an unref for each removal operation. This may result in a uaf
when we attempt the second unref.

This change fixes the race by making __mctp_key_remove tolerant to being
called on a key that has already been removed from the socket/net lists,
and only performs the unref when we do the actual remove. We also need
to hold the list lock on the ioctl cleanup path.

This fix is based on a bug report and comprehensive analysis from
butt3rflyh4ck <butterflyhuangxx@gmail.com>, found via syzkaller.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 63ed1aab3d40 ("mctp: Add SIOCMCTP{ALLOC,DROP}TAG ioctls for tag control")
Reported-by: butt3rflyh4ck <butterflyhuangxx@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jeremy Kerr <jk@codeconstruct.com.au>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\thlist_del(&key->hlist);', '\thlist_del(&key->sklist);', '', '\t/* unref for the lists */', '\tmctp_key_unref(key);'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!hlist_unhashed(&key->hlist)) {', '\t\thlist_del_init(&key->hlist);', '\t\thlist_del_init(&key->sklist);', '\t\t/* unref for the lists */', '\t\tmctp_key_unref(key);', '\t}']}
description: A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel MCTP (Management Component Transport Protocol) functionality. This issue occurs when a user simultaneously calls DROPTAG ioctl and socket close happens, which could allow a local user to crash the system or potentially escalate their privileges on the system.

code_evidence: After releasing key->lock, __mctp_key_remove unconditionally calls hlist_del on key->hlist and key->sklist and then mctp_key_unref(key). If a concurrent path (socket close vs. DROPTAG ioctl) already removed the key from these lists and dropped the list reference, these hlist_del and unref operations act on an already-freed/released key. The unref may free the key a second time, and the subsequent kfree_skb at line 17 runs after the object may be gone.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the code dereferences and mutates a key object after its reference may already have been dropped and the memory freed; the missing hashed-state guard permits the second removal to touch freed memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: no check that the key is still linked before deleting from lists and dropping the list reference. Trigger: simultaneous DROPTAG ioctl and socket close both reach removal for the same key. Consequence: double unref frees the key while still in use, yielding a use-after-free that can crash the kernel or potentially enable privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
[gsm] Delay the creation of the GsmXSMPClient until it really exists

We used to create the GsmXSMPClient before the XSMP connection is really
accepted. This can lead to some issues, though. An example is:
https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=598211#c19. Quoting:

 "What is happening is that a new client (probably metacity in your
 case) is opening an ICE connection in the GSM_MANAGER_PHASE_END_SESSION
 phase, which causes a new GsmXSMPClient to be added to the client
 store. The GSM_MANAGER_PHASE_EXIT phase then begins before the client
 has had a chance to establish a xsmp connection, which means that
 client->priv->conn will not be initialized at the point that xsmp_stop
 is called on the new unregistered client."

The fix is to create the GsmXSMPClient object when there's a real XSMP
connection. This implies moving the timeout that makes sure we don't
have an empty client to the XSMP server.

https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=598211
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        IceConn        ice_conn;', '        GsmXSMPClient *client;', '        client = ice_conn->context;', '        g_return_val_if_fail (client != NULL, TRUE);', '        gsm_xsmp_client_connect (client, sms_conn, mask_ret, callbacks_ret);'], 'added_lines': ['        IceConn                ice_conn;', '        GsmClient             *client;', '        GsmIceConnectionWatch *data;', '        data = ice_conn->context;', '        /* Each GsmXSMPClient has its own IceConn watcher */', '        free_ice_connection_watch (data);', '        client = gsm_xsmp_client_new (ice_conn);', '', '        gsm_store_add (server->priv->client_store, gsm_client_peek_id (client), G_OBJECT (client));', '        /* the store will own the ref */', '        g_object_unref (client);', '', '        gsm_xsmp_client_connect (GSM_XSMP_CLIENT (client), sms_conn, mask_ret, callbacks_ret);']}
description: Bad reference counting in the context of accept_ice_connection() in gsm-xsmp-server.c in old versions of gnome-session up until version 2.29.92 allows a local attacker to establish ICE connections to gnome-session with invalid authentication data (an invalid magic cookie). Each failed authentication attempt will leak a file descriptor in gnome-session. When the maximum number of file descriptors is exhausted in the gnome-session process, it will enter an infinite loop trying to communicate without success, consuming 100% of the CPU. The graphical session associated with the gnome-session process will stop working correctly, because communication with gnome-session is no longer possible.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function contains no loop or iteration construct; it only performs null-check, lookup, and connect calls, so it cannot directly support an infinite-loop weakness.

commit_msg:
Bug 703366: Fix double free of object during linearization.

This appears to happen because we parse an illegal object from
a broken file and assign it to object 0, which is defined to
be free.

Here, we fix the parsing code so this can't happen.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (gen < 0 || gen >= 65536)', '\t{', '\t\tif (try_repair)', '\t\t\t*try_repair = 1;', '\t\tfz_throw(ctx, FZ_ERROR_SYNTAX, "invalid generation number (%d)", gen);', '\t}']}
description: A flaw was found in mupdf 1.18.0. Double free of object during linearization may lead to memory corruption and other potential consequences.

code_evidence: Line 30 assigns the parsed generation number gen = buf->i with no range check; a broken file can supply an out-of-range generation value for an indirect object reference.
Lines 80-113 wrap stream/endobj handling in fz_try; on exception the catch at 109-113 calls pdf_drop_obj(ctx, obj) and rethrows, so any object already created and stored in obj is dropped once here.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's error path at lines 109-113 explicitly frees obj via pdf_drop_obj and rethrows; combined with malformed object identity from the unchecked gen at line 30, the object can be freed again elsewhere, matching CWE-415's double free of the same address. This is a double-free consequence rather than merely improper input validation (CWE-20).

evidence_lines.code:
gen = buf->i;
tok = pdf_lex(ctx, file, buf);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser accepts an unvalidated generation number from the file and builds an object (possibly an indirect reference) whose identity is malformed, so the same object can be registered/assigned in a way that aliases a free object entry. Trigger: a crafted PDF with an illegal generation number in an indirect object header. When later processing frees that aliased object, pdf_drop_obj is invoked twice on the same address, causing memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Prevent `CHECK`-fail when decoding resource handles from proto

In certain scenarios, the proto might contain tensors that have too many elements (overflow). This is a `CHECK`-fail in general, but we should prevent this, given how many CVEs caused by that we have received this year (a large fraction of 200).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 408049766
Change-Id: I2ac20b247aa8ed9110846fbdb7a0a9401f2c168c
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    ps[i].FromProto(proto);'], 'added_lines': ['    if (!ps[i].FromProto(proto).ok()) {', '      return false;', '    }']}
description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. When decoding a resource handle tensor from protobuf, a TensorFlow process can encounter cases where a `CHECK` assertion is invalidated based on user controlled arguments. This allows attackers to cause denial of services in TensorFlow processes. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: The loop parses each attacker-controlled serialized ResourceHandleProto from the decoder buffer (line 7) and previously called ps[i].FromProto(proto) (line 10) without checking its result. FromProto can fail on user-controlled proto contents (e.g., element-count overflow), and the unchecked call propagated into an internal CHECK-failing path instead of returning false.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-617 fits because a reachable assertion (CHECK) is invalidated by user-controlled input, causing abnormal process termination. This is not merely improper input validation; the distinguishing consequence is the fatal assertion leading to DoS.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return status of FromProto is ignored, so a malformed/oversized proto reaching the resource-handle conversion triggers an internal CHECK assertion rather than a graceful failure. Trigger: attacker-supplied serialized proto with overflowing tensor element counts. Consequence: process abort/denial of service.

commit_msg:
fix unbalanced page refcounting in bio_map_user_iov

bio_map_user_iov and bio_unmap_user do unbalanced pages refcounting if
IO vector has small consecutive buffers belonging to the same page.
bio_add_pc_page merges them into one, but the page reference is never
dropped.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Vitaly Mayatskikh <v.mayatskih@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tunsigned short prev_bi_vcnt = bio->bi_vcnt;', '', '\t\t\t/*', '\t\t\t * check if vector was merged with previous', '\t\t\t * drop page reference if needed', '\t\t\t */', '\t\t\tif (bio->bi_vcnt == prev_bi_vcnt)', '\t\t\t\tput_page(pages[j]);']}
description: The bio_map_user_iov and bio_unmap_user functions in block/bio.c in the Linux kernel before 4.13.8 do unbalanced refcounting when a SCSI I/O vector has small consecutive buffers belonging to the same page. The bio_add_pc_page function merges them into one, but the page reference is never dropped. This causes a memory leak and possible system lockup (exploitable against the host OS by a guest OS user, if a SCSI disk is passed through to a virtual machine) due to an out-of-memory condition.

code_evidence: The loop over pages calls bio_add_pc_page for each page and, on failure or when bytes < requested, breaks; the remaining pages are released via put_page in the while loop. When bio_add_pc_page merges a consecutive buffer into the previous bvec (returning bytes but not adding a bvec), pages[j]'s reference obtained from get_user_pages_fast is never dropped, since j advances and the page is not in the tail-release range.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the function fails to release references to a limited kernel resource (pages) under a specific input pattern, producing unbounded memory consumption. It is not a simple logic bug alone; the supported impact is resource exhaustion leading to denial of service.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code assumes every successfully added page produces a new bio vector, so it does not put_page a page whose buffer was merged into the previous bvec. Trigger: an I/O vector with small consecutive buffers on the same page. Consequence: leaked page references accumulate, causing memory exhaustion and possible system lockup/DoS.

description: In PHP before 5.5.32, 5.6.x before 5.6.18, and 7.x before 7.0.3, all of the return values of stream_get_meta_data can be controlled if the input can be controlled (e.g., during file uploads). For example, a "$uri = stream_get_meta_data(fopen($file, "r"))['uri']" call mishandles the case where $file is data:text/plain;uri=eviluri, -- in other words, metadata can be set by an attacker.

commit_msg:
misc: sgi-gru: fix use-after-free error in gru_set_context_option, gru_fault and gru_handle_user_call_os

In some bad situation, the gts may be freed gru_check_chiplet_assignment.
The call chain can be gru_unload_context->gru_free_gru_context->gts_drop
and kfree finally. However, the caller didn't know if the gts is freed
or not and use it afterwards. This will trigger a Use after Free bug.

Fix it by introducing a return value to see if it's in error path or not.
Free the gts in caller if gru_check_chiplet_assignment check failed.

Fixes: 55484c45dbec ("gru: allow users to specify gru chiplet 2")
Signed-off-by: Zheng Wang <zyytlz.wz@163.com>
Acked-by: Dimitri Sivanich <sivanich@hpe.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20221110035033.19498-1-zyytlz.wz@163.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tgru_check_context_placement(gts);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif (gru_check_context_placement(gts)) {', '\t\t\t\tgru_unlock_gts(gts);', '\t\t\t\tgru_unload_context(gts, 1);', '\t\t\t\treturn ret;', '\t\t\t}']}
description: A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s SGI GRU driver in the way the first gru_file_unlocked_ioctl function is called by the user, where a fail pass occurs in the gru_check_chiplet_assignment function. This flaw allows a local user to crash or potentially escalate their privileges on the system.

code_evidence: The sco_blade_chiplet branch stores user-supplied blade/chiplet ids into gts->ts_user_blade_id and ts_user_chiplet_id, then calls gru_check_context_placement(gts) without checking its outcome.
After the switch, gru_unlock_gts(gts) is called unconditionally and the function returns, even though gru_check_context_placement may have freed gts on a failed chiplet-assignment check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function references a gts pointer that may already have been freed by gru_check_context_placement, matching CWE-416 (use after free). This is not merely a missing error code; the defect is continued use of freed memory, which the patch prevents by returning on the error path.

evidence_lines.code:
gru_unlock_gts(gts);
return ret;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return status of gru_check_context_placement is discarded, so the caller cannot detect the error path where gts is dropped/freed. Trigger: a local user issues the ioctl with a blade/chiplet combination that fails the chiplet-assignment check. The stale gts is then passed to gru_unlock_gts and returned to the caller, yielding a use-after-free (crash or possible corruption).

commit_msg:
netfilter: x_tables: check for bogus target offset

We're currently asserting that targetoff + targetsize <= nextoff.

Extend it to also check that targetoff is >= sizeof(xt_entry).
Since this is generic code, add an argument pointing to the start of the
match/target, we can then derive the base structure size from the delta.

We also need the e->elems pointer in a followup change to validate matches.

Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t   const char *elems,', '\tlong size_of_base_struct = elems - (const char *)base;', '', '\t/* target start is within the ip/ip6/arpt_entry struct */', '\tif (target_offset < size_of_base_struct)', '\t\treturn -EINVAL;']}
description: The compat IPT_SO_SET_REPLACE and IP6T_SO_SET_REPLACE setsockopt implementations in the netfilter subsystem in the Linux kernel before 4.6.3 allow local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (memory corruption) by leveraging in-container root access to provide a crafted offset value that triggers an unintended decrement.

commit_msg:
util: Check for NULL string in writefile

This check was there previously, but was removed in f549b757 with
the addition of a check during parse that every rule has rspfile
if and only if it has rspfile_content. However, this fails to
consider the possibility of those variables coming from the edge
or global environment. So, re-add the check.

Fixes #67.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (fwrite(s->s, 1, s->n, f) != s->n || fflush(f) != 0) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (s && (fwrite(s->s, 1, s->n, f) != s->n || fflush(f) != 0)) {']}
description: samurai 1.2 has a NULL pointer dereference in writefile() in util.c via a crafted build file.

code_evidence: Line 12 dereferences s via s->s and s->n in fwrite without first checking whether s is NULL, so a NULL string argument causes a NULL pointer dereference before any error handling.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the function directly dereferences a pointer expected to be valid but which can be NULL. This is a straightforward NULL pointer dereference, not a buffer overflow or use-after-free, since the flaw is the missing NULL check before member access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: writefile() assumes its string pointer s is non-NULL and reads s->s/s->n unconditionally. Trigger: a caller passes NULL, e.g. when rspfile/rspfile_content come from edge or global environment. Consequence: crash (DoS) from dereferencing NULL; no bounds or validity check guards the access.

commit_msg:
Fix an illegal memory access when parsing an ELF file containing corrupt symbol version information.

	PR 29699
	* elf.c (_bfd_elf_slurp_version_tables): Fail if the sh_info field
	of the section header is zero.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      elf_tdata (abfd)->verref = (Elf_Internal_Verneed *) bfd_alloc (abfd, amt);'], 'added_lines': ['      if (amt == 0)', '\tgoto error_return_verref;', '      elf_tdata (abfd)->verref = (Elf_Internal_Verneed *) bfd_zalloc (abfd, amt);']}
description: An illegal memory access flaw was found in the binutils package. Parsing an ELF file containing corrupt symbol version information may result in a denial of service. This issue is the result of an incomplete fix for CVE-2020-16599.

code_evidence: The only guard on hdr->sh_info is a division-based bound check; it does not reject sh_info == 0, so amt computed at line 31 can be zero.
bfd_alloc with amt == 0 may return NULL, and the code then jumps to error_return_verref, leaving verref NULL while returning false to the caller.

The loop at line 44 iterates i < hdr->sh_info with iverneed derived from verref; when sh_info is zero the loop is skipped and cverrefs is set, so downstream consumers may use a NULL/empty verref array.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw permits a NULL verref pointer to be stored and later dereferenced by callers, matching CWE-476. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read, since the missing zero-count constraint is what lets the NULL pointer propagate.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing rejection of a corrupt sh_info == 0, producing a zero-size allocation for verref. Trigger: a crafted ELF .gnu.version_r section with sh_info zero. Consequence: verref is NULL (or an empty array) while parsing continues, so later version-symbol lookups dereference a NULL pointer, causing an illegal memory access/DoS.

commit_msg:
flow_dissector: Jump to exit code in __skb_flow_dissect

Instead of returning immediately (on a parsing failure for instance) we
jump to cleanup code. This always sets protocol values in key_control
(even on a failure there is still valid information in the key_tags that
was set before the problem was hit).

Signed-off-by: Tom Herbert <tom@herbertland.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\treturn false;', '\t\t\treturn false;', '\t\t\treturn false;', '\t\t\treturn false;', '\t\t\treturn false;', '\t\t\treturn false;', '\t\tkey_basic->n_proto = proto;', '\t\tkey_control->thoff = (u16)nhoff;', '\t\treturn true;', '\t\t\treturn false;', '\t\t\tkey_basic->n_proto = proto;', '\t\t\tkey_basic->ip_proto = ip_proto;', '\t\t\tkey_control->thoff = (u16)nhoff;', '', '\t\t\treturn true;', '\t\t}', '', '\t\treturn true;', '\t\treturn false;', '\t\t\treturn false;', '\t\t\t\treturn false;', '\t\t\t\treturn false;', '\t\t\treturn false;', '\tkey_basic->n_proto = proto;', '\tkey_basic->ip_proto = ip_proto;', '\tkey_control->thoff = (u16)nhoff;', '', '\treturn true;'], 'added_lines': ['\tbool ret = false;', '\t\t\tgoto out_bad;', '\t\t\tgoto out_bad;', '\t\t\tgoto out_bad;', '\t\t\tgoto out_bad;', '\t\t\tgoto out_bad;', '\t\t\tgoto out_bad;', '\t\tgoto out_good;', '\t\t\tgoto out_bad;', '\t\t\tgoto out_good;', '\t\t}', '', '\t\tgoto out_good;', '\t\tgoto out_bad;', '\t\t\tgoto out_bad;', '\t\t\t\tgoto out_bad;', '\t\t\t\tgoto out_bad;', '\t\t\tgoto out_bad;', 'out_good:', '\tret = true;', '', 'out_bad:', '\tkey_basic->n_proto = proto;', '\tkey_basic->ip_proto = ip_proto;', '\tkey_control->thoff = (u16)nhoff;', '', '\treturn ret;']}
description: The __skb_flow_dissect function in net/core/flow_dissector.c in the Linux kernel before 4.3 does not ensure that n_proto, ip_proto, and thoff are initialized, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (system crash) or possibly execute arbitrary code via a single crafted MPLS packet.

code_evidence: ip_proto is initialized to 0 at declaration [12]. In the MPLS entropy branch, n_proto, ip_proto and thoff are written only inside the entropy check [163,164,165]; the non-entropy path returns true at [168] without setting them. The normal exit path [248,249,250] also writes these key fields, but every earlier `return false`/`return true` exits (e.g. [42,64,94,122,143,152,168,173]) bypasses that block entirely.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is improper initialization: output fields in the key structures are not set on all control-flow paths before the function reports success/failure. This matches CWE-665 rather than a memory-safety CWE, since the defect is missing initialization of resource fields, with DoS/crash as the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function returns directly from many parse branches, so the key_basic->n_proto/ip_proto and key_control->thoff fields are left uninitialized when parsing fails or takes an early success path. A crafted MPLS packet can trigger one of these early returns, causing consumers to read uninitialized key data, leading to a crash or misuse of the key values.

LTE RRC: fix a memory leak in composite TVB handling

Bug: 16341
Change-Id: Ib6c020ea3df8b39a02f742f0684fca7db96f1fc3
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/35899
Petri-Dish: Pascal Quantin <pascal@wireshark.org>
Tested-by: Petri Dish Buildbot
Reviewed-by: Pascal Quantin <pascal@wireshark.org>
(cherry picked from commit adeeb7f2da801303768ce96e2cacf6a703a69c6f)
Conflicts:
	epan/dissectors/packet-lte-rrc.c
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/35903
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        tvb_composite_append(si_tvb, tvb_new_real_data(pd, 1, 1));', '        tvb_composite_append(gsm_rlcmac_dl_tvb, tvb_new_real_data(pd, 1, 1));'], 'added_lines': ['        tvb_composite_append(si_tvb, tvb_new_child_real_data(tvb, pd, 1, 1));', '        tvb_composite_append(gsm_rlcmac_dl_tvb, tvb_new_child_real_data(tvb, pd, 1, 1));']}
description: In Wireshark 3.2.0 to 3.2.1, 3.0.0 to 3.0.8, and 2.6.0 to 2.6.14, the LTE RRC dissector could leak memory. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-lte-rrc.c by adjusting certain append operations.

code_evidence: A composite tvbuff si_tvb is created and a real-data tvb wrapping the wmem_alloc'd 1-byte buffer pd is appended (line 15), then finalized and registered via add_new_data_source before being passed to lte_rrc_call_dissector.
The same pattern for gsm_rlcmac_dl_tvb: a standalone real-data tvb is appended to the composite (line 27) and the composite is finalized and added as a data source.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates a real-data tvb whose lifetime is not tracked by any parent, so the allocation is not released after use, matching CWE-401 (missing release of memory after effective lifetime). The fix switches to tvb_new_child_real_data so the child is freed with its parent, confirming the ownership/leak root cause rather than a use-after-free or bounds issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the appended child tvb is created with tvb_new_real_data, so it is not tied to the parent tvb's lifetime and has no owner to free it. When the composite tvb is later freed or the dissector aborts, the child real-data tvb (and its backing buffer) is never released, leaking memory per dissection. Trigger: processing SystemInfoListGERAN items with the gsm_a_dtap or gsm_rlcmac handle registered. Consequence: unbounded memory growth / DoS.

commit_msg:
Both aac_send_raw_srb() and aac_get_hba_info() may copy stack allocated
structs to userspace without initializing all members of these
structs. Clear out this memory to prevent information leaks.

Fixes: 423400e64d377 ("scsi: aacraid: Include HBA direct interface")
Fixes: c799d519bf088 ("scsi: aacraid: Retrieve HBA host information ioctl")
Signed-off-by: Seth Forshee <seth.forshee@canonical.com>
Reviewed-by: Johannes Thumshirn <jthumshirn@suse.de>
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tmemset(&hbainfo, 0, sizeof(hbainfo));']}
description: An issue was discovered in drivers/scsi/aacraid/commctrl.c in the Linux kernel before 4.13. There is potential exposure of kernel stack memory because aac_send_raw_srb does not initialize the reply structure.

code_evidence: Line 3 declares a stack-allocated struct aac_hba_info hbainfo. Lines 4-11 assign only eight specific members (adapter_number, system_io_bus_number, device_number, function_number, vendor_id, device_id, sub_vendor_id, sub_system_id) but never zero-initialize the whole struct, leaving any padding and unassigned members holding prior stack contents. Line 12 then copies the full sizeof(struct aac_hba_info) bytes to a userspace pointer arg via copy_to_user.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function explicitly transfers partially uninitialized kernel stack data to a user-controlled buffer, exposing sensitive internal memory to an unauthorized actor, which matches CWE-200's exposure of sensitive information. The added memset confirms the missing initialization is the flaw rather than a generic memory-safety issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the reply struct is partially initialized on the stack and its full size is copied to userspace, so uninitialized bytes (padding and any fields not set) are disclosed. Trigger: a user invokes the ioctl path calling aac_get_hba_info; the consequence is exposure of residual kernel stack memory to an unprivileged caller, a confidentiality leak.

commit_msg:
avformat/rl2: Fix DoS due to lack of eof check

Fixes: loop.rl2

Found-by: Xiaohei and Wangchu from Alibaba Security Team
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    for(i=0; i < frame_count;i++)', '    for(i=0; i < frame_count;i++)', '    for(i=0; i < frame_count;i++)'], 'added_lines': ['    for(i=0; i < frame_count;i++) {', '        if (avio_feof(pb))', '            return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;', '    }', '    for(i=0; i < frame_count;i++) {', '        if (avio_feof(pb))', '            return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;', '    }', '    for(i=0; i < frame_count;i++) {', '        if (avio_feof(pb))', '            return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;', '    }']}
description: In libavformat/rl2.c in FFmpeg 3.3.3, a DoS in rl2_read_header() due to lack of an EOF (End of File) check might cause huge CPU and memory consumption. When a crafted RL2 file, which claims a large "frame_count" field in the header but does not contain sufficient backing data, is provided, the loops (for offset and size tables) would consume huge CPU and memory resources, since there is no EOF check inside these loops.

code_evidence: frame_count is read from the file at line 25 and only checked against INT_MAX/sizeof(uint32_t) at line 26, bounding allocation size but not the number of iterations against available input.
Lines 78-83 iterate i < frame_count three times, calling avio_rl32(pb) per iteration with no EOF check; if the file lacks backing data, avio_rl32 returns values without terminating the loops.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-834 fits because the iteration count is set by an untrusted header field and not sufficiently limited relative to input, enabling resource-consumption DoS. This is excessive iteration rather than a memory-safety flaw; the missing EOF check is the specific mechanism.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop bound frame_count is attacker-controlled from the header and is not constrained by the actual remaining input length. A crafted RL2 file declaring a large frame_count but containing little data causes the three table-reading loops to run their full count, consuming excessive CPU (and driving the prior allocations).

commit_msg:
drbg: ensure fork-safety without using a pthread_atfork handler

When the new OpenSSL CSPRNG was introduced in version 1.1.1,
it was announced in the release notes that it would be fork-safe,
which the old CSPRNG hadn't been.

The fork-safety was implemented using a fork count, which was
incremented by a pthread_atfork handler. Initially, this handler
was enabled by default. Unfortunately, the default behaviour
had to be changed for other reasons in commit b5319bdbd095, so
the new OpenSSL CSPRNG failed to keep its promise.

This commit restores the fork-safety using a different approach.
It replaces the fork count by a fork id, which coincides with
the process id on UNIX-like operating systems and is zero on other
operating systems. It is used to detect when an automatic reseed
after a fork is necessary.

To prevent a future regression, it also adds a test to verify that
the child reseeds after fork.

CVE-2019-1549

Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <paul.dale@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/9802)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    drbg->fork_count = rand_fork_count;'], 'added_lines': ['    drbg->fork_id = openssl_get_fork_id();']}
description: OpenSSL 1.1.1 introduced a rewritten random number generator (RNG). This was intended to include protection in the event of a fork() system call in order to ensure that the parent and child processes did not share the same RNG state. However this protection was not being used in the default case. A partial mitigation for this issue is that the output from a high precision timer is mixed into the RNG state so the likelihood of a parent and child process sharing state is significantly reduced. If an application already calls OPENSSL_init_crypto() explicitly using OPENSSL_INIT_ATFORK then this problem does not occur at all. Fixed in OpenSSL 1.1.1d (Affected 1.1.1-1.1.1c).

code_evidence: The constructor allocates a RAND_DRBG object with zeroed memory via OPENSSL_zalloc/OPENSSL_secure_zalloc.
Line 13 initializes the DRBG's fork tracking field from the global rand_fork_count rather than from a per-process identifier.
Line 14 stores the parent pointer, establishing the DRBG state whose fork-safety depends on the fork tracking value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function seeds the DRBG's fork-safety state from a value that fails to change across fork, so the DRBG can emit duplicate random values; this is insufficiently random output in a security context, matching CWE-330. It is not a memory-safety or locking flaw, but a failure to ensure unpredictable/independent random state.

evidence_lines.code:
RAND_DRBG *drbg = secure ? OPENSSL_secure_zalloc(sizeof(*drbg))
: OPENSSL_zalloc(sizeof(*drbg));
drbg->fork_count = rand_fork_count;
drbg->parent = parent;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: fork detection relies on a global fork count (rand_fork_count) that is only maintained when the pthread_atfork handler is enabled, which is not the default. Trigger: an application forks without OPENSSL_INIT_ATFORK, so the child inherits the parent's DRBG state with an unchanged fork count. Consequence: parent and child may produce identical random output, weakening the CSPRNG's unpredictability in a security context.

commit_msg:
Re: readelf: Consolidate --syms --use-dynamic with --dyn-syms

	PR 25821
	* readelf.c (get_num_dynamic_syms): Typo fix.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t      buckets = NULL;'], 'added_lines': ['\t      chains = NULL;']}
description: A double free vulnerability exists in the Binary File Descriptor (BFD) (aka libbrd) in GNU Binutils 2.35 in the process_symbol_table, as demonstrated in readelf, via a crafted file.

code_evidence: When num_of_syms is zero, the code frees buckets and sets buckets = NULL, correctly preventing a later free of that pointer.
In the following block the code frees chains but assigns buckets = NULL instead of chains = NULL, leaving chains pointing to freed memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-415 fits because the mis-nulled pointer leaves chains freed but still referenced, so a later free() on chains frees the same address twice. It is distinct from a mere NULL-pointer mistake: the defect is duplicate release of one allocation, not a null dereference.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the cleanup after freeing chains nulls the wrong pointer (buckets), so chains remains dangling. Trigger: num_of_syms == 0 with a non-NULL chains pointer, causing this cleanup path to run; a subsequent free of chains (or reuse of the stale pointer) yields a double free/use-after-free. The supported consequence is memory corruption (integrity) and possible crash (availability), with code-execution risk in principle.

commit_msg:
9pfs: fix potential host memory leak in v9fs_read

In 9pfs read dispatch function, it doesn't free two QEMUIOVector
object thus causing potential memory leak. This patch avoid this.

Signed-off-by: Li Qiang <liqiang6-s@360.cn>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kurz <groug@kaod.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                goto out;', '            goto out;'], 'added_lines': ['                goto out_free_iovec;', '            goto out_free_iovec;', 'out_free_iovec:']}
description: Memory leak in the v9fs_read function in hw/9pfs/9p.c in QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) allows local guest OS administrators to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) via vectors related to an I/O read operation.

code_evidence: Lines 40-41 allocate qiov_full and qiov via v9fs_init_qiov_from_pdu and qemu_iovec_init. On preadv failure (55-58) and marshalling failure (60-63), control jumps to out without reaching the qemu_iovec_destroy calls at 65-66, so both iovec resources are never released on those error paths.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates QEMUIOVector resources whose lifetime ends on the error path but never releases them, matching CWE-772's missing release after effective lifetime. This is a resource-release defect, not an out-of-bounds or use-after-free issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: error exits from the read loop or pdu_marshal bypass the iovec destruction block. Trigger: a guest-issued read that causes v9fs_co_preadv to return a negative length or pdu_marshal to fail. Consequence: qiov and qiov_full are leaked per invocation, enabling guest-driven host memory exhaustion (DoS).

commit_msg:
x86: limit linear page table use to a single level

That's the only way that they're meant to be used. Without such a
restriction arbitrarily long chains of same-level page tables can be
built, tearing down of which may then cause arbitrarily deep recursion,
causing a stack overflow. To facilitate this restriction, a counter is
being introduced to track both the number of same-level entries in a
page table as well as the number of uses of a page table in another
same-level one (counting into positive and negative direction
respectively, utilizing the fact that both counts can't be non-zero at
the same time).

Note that the added accounting introduces a restriction on the number
of times a page can be used in other same-level page tables - more than
32k of such uses are no longer possible.

Note also that some put_page_and_type[_preemptible]() calls are
replaced with open-coded equivalents.  This seemed preferrable to
adding "parent_table" to the matrix of functions.

Note further that cross-domain same-level page table references are no
longer permitted (they probably never should have been).

This is XSA-240.

Reported-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: George Dunlap <george.dunlap@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        return put_page_type_preemptible(pg);', '    return put_page_and_type_preemptible(pg);'], 'added_lines': ['    int rc;', '        return _put_page_type(pg, true, mfn_to_page(_mfn(pfn)));', '        current->arch.old_guest_ptpg = mfn_to_page(_mfn(pfn));', '    rc = _put_page_type(pg, true, mfn_to_page(_mfn(pfn)));', '    if ( likely(!rc) )', '        put_page(pg);', '', '    return rc;']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.9.x allowing x86 PV guest OS users to cause a denial of service (unbounded recursion, stack consumption, and hypervisor crash) or possibly gain privileges via crafted page-table stacking.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function only performs reference/page-type release for L3 entries; it contains no allocation or accounting logic that limits same-level page-table stacking, so it does not itself demonstrate the uncontrolled resource consumption described by CWE-400.

commit_msg:
Flush secureRandom buffer on fork

Summary: On fork, flush the secureRandom buffer, so that we don't share entropy between the parent and child.

Reviewed By: ricklavoie

Differential Revision: D9196474

fbshipit-source-id: 12ff8488d814466186df61328a5f1d4000beb27f

commit_msg:
Fix 697172: degenerate labeled break/continue statement.

A labeled break statement will look for a matching label through
its chain of parent statements. We start looking at the break statement
though, so if the label is attached to the break, we'll return the break
statement itself as a break target.

Start looking for targets one level up instead.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\ttarget = breaktarget(J, F, stm, stm->a->string);', '\t\t\ttarget = breaktarget(J, F, stm, NULL);', '\t\t\ttarget = continuetarget(J, F, stm, stm->a->string);', '\t\t\ttarget = continuetarget(J, F, stm, NULL);', '\t\ttarget = returntarget(J, F, stm);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\ttarget = breaktarget(J, F, stm->parent, stm->a->string);', '\t\t\ttarget = breaktarget(J, F, stm->parent, NULL);', '\t\t\ttarget = continuetarget(J, F, stm->parent, stm->a->string);', '\t\t\ttarget = continuetarget(J, F, stm->parent, NULL);', '\t\ttarget = returntarget(J, F, stm->parent);']}
description: Artifex Software, Inc. MuJS before 5008105780c0b0182ea6eda83ad5598f225be3ee allows context-dependent attackers to conduct "denial of service (application crash)" attacks by using the "malformed labeled break/continue in JavaScript" approach, related to a "NULL pointer dereference" issue affecting the jscompile.c component.

code_evidence: For STM_BREAK, breaktarget is called with stm itself as the starting node; a label attached to the break statement makes breaktarget return stm as the target. cexit then records that target and addjump uses it without a NULL check, so a degenerate labeled break yields an invalid target.
STM_CONTINUE mirrors this: continuetarget is started at stm, so a label on the continue statement resolves to the continue itself, and cexit/addjump consume the resulting target.
STM_RETURN passes stm to returntarget, which searches upward from the return statement rather than its parent.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The described defect is a dereference of a pointer expected valid but found NULL, fitting CWE-476. It is not merely a logic error in label resolution; the resolution failure propagates to an unchecked pointer use causing a crash.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the target-search helpers start at the break/continue/return statement itself instead of its parent, so a label attached to that statement matches itself and produces a degenerate or NULL target. Trigger: malformed labeled break/continue (or return) in JavaScript. Consequence: the target is consumed by cexit/addjump without validation, leading to a NULL pointer dereference and compiler crash (DoS).

commit_msg: HTTP/2: per-iteration stream handling limit.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (h2c->new_streams++ >= 2 * h2scf->concurrent_streams) {', '        ngx_log_error(NGX_LOG_INFO, h2c->connection->log, 0,', '                      "client sent too many streams at once");', '', '        status = NGX_HTTP_V2_REFUSED_STREAM;', '        goto rst_stream;', '    }', '', '    if (h2c->refused_streams++ > ngx_max(h2scf->concurrent_streams, 100)) {', '        ngx_log_error(NGX_LOG_INFO, h2c->connection->log, 0,', '                      "client sent too many refused streams");', '        return ngx_http_v2_connection_error(h2c, NGX_HTTP_V2_NO_ERROR);', '    }', '']}
description: The HTTP/2 protocol allows a denial of service (server resource consumption) because request cancellation can reset many streams quickly, as exploited in the wild in August through October 2023.

code_evidence: The concurrent-stream check at [93-98] compares h2c->processing against concurrent_streams and jumps to rst_stream on exceedance, but the function then continues allocating per-stream state: ngx_http_v2_get_node_by_id ([109-112]) and ngx_http_v2_create_stream ([117-120]), each allocating nodes/pools/streams tied to the client-supplied stream identifier.

Each HEADERS frame with a fresh odd sid passes the [70-82] identifier validation and reaches the allocation path; refused streams merely send RST_STREAM at [146-150] and return to header-block parsing, so the client controls how many allocations and resets occur per connection.

The function tracks only h2c->processing, not cumulative per-iteration stream creation, so a client can open and cancel many streams quickly; the reset path at [146-150] returns without any per-connection rate/creation cap.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the function is expected to track and restrict client-driven HTTP/2 stream resources but lacks an effective limit on cumulative creation/reset activity, allowing resource exhaustion. It is not merely a protocol-validation bug (e.g., CWE-20): the identifier checks at [70-82] are present, while the missing constraint is on resource consumption.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function throttles only the instantaneous count of processing streams, not the rate or total number of stream allocations and RST_STREAM resets a client can trigger. Trigger: a peer rapidly sends HEADERS frames with increasing odd stream IDs and cancels them, driving repeated node/stream allocation and reset handling. Supported consequence: unbounded per-connection resource consumption (memory/CPU), enabling denial of service.

description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.3 and 2.2.0 to 2.2.11, the JSON, XML, NTP, XMPP, and GDB dissectors could crash. This was addressed in epan/tvbparse.c by limiting the recursion depth.

code_evidence: Line 8 bounds-checks offset plus the subelement length against tt->end_offset, returning -1 if exceeded (line 9). Line 11 recursively invokes the subelement's condition callback with target_offset++, and line 12 loops while len < 0 and target_offset+1 < tt->end_offset. The recursion is depth-controlled only by the loop bound, not by a recursion counter in this function; the added recursion_depth check is absent from this version.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Unbounded recursion causes writes past the stack buffer boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. The missing recursion-depth constraint is the specific cause; the stack overflow and corruption are the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: cond_until recursively calls wanted->control.until.subelem->condition without any recursion-depth limit, so nested until-conditions driven by attacker-supplied packet data recurse until the process stack is exhausted. Trigger: a crafted packet parsed by a dissector using tvbparse with deeply nested until constructs. Consequence: stack overflow, leading to crash or potential memory corruption beyond the intended stack buffer.

commit_msg: Catch SGI buffer overruns
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                if(expandrow(&state->buffer[c->channo], &ptr[c->rleoffset], c->rlelength, im->bands))', '                    goto sgi_finish_decode;', '                if(expandrow2(&state->buffer[c->channo * 2], &ptr[c->rleoffset], c->rlelength, im->bands))', '                    goto sgi_finish_decode;'], 'added_lines': ['    int status;', '                status = expandrow(&state->buffer[c->channo], &ptr[c->rleoffset], c->rlelength, im->bands, im->xsize);', '                status = expandrow2(&state->buffer[c->channo * 2], &ptr[c->rleoffset], c->rlelength, im->bands, im->xsize);', '            }', '            if (status == -1) {', '                state->errcode = IMAGING_CODEC_OVERRUN;', '                return -1;', '            } else if (status == 1) {', '                goto sgi_finish_decode;']}
description: libImaging/SgiRleDecode.c in Pillow before 6.2.2 has an SGI buffer overflow.

code_evidence: Row/channel RLE offset and length are read from the file-controlled tables; only an offset+length check against bufsize is performed before decode.
expandrow/expandrow2 copy RLE data into state->buffer at c->channo (or channo*2) without passing im->xsize, so the per-row output capacity is not enforced; return value only triggers goto.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because file-controlled input is copied into a fixed output buffer without verifying input size against output size; the destination-width constraint is missing. This is a write overflow, not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the RLE decompressors write decoded row data into state->buffer without knowing the destination row width (im->xsize), so a crafted SGI RLE length/offset can produce more output than the allocated row buffer. Trigger: malicious file tables drive expandrow/expandrow2. Consequence: heap buffer overflow, memory corruption/crash.

commit_msg:
PyACL - Fixing integer overflows that occur when resizing ACLs

Fixes #1700
CVE-2021-32559
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        unsigned short required_size = psacl->AclSize + sizeof(SYSTEM_AUDIT_ACE) + (unsigned short)GetLengthSid(psid);', '        psacl_padded = (ACL *)malloc(required_size);', '        if (psacl_padded == NULL)', '            return PyErr_Format(PyExc_MemoryError, "AddAuditAccessAce: unable to allocated %d bytes", required_size);', '', '        psacl_padded->AclSize = required_size;'], 'added_lines': ['        unsigned int required_size = psacl->AclSize + sizeof(SYSTEM_AUDIT_ACE) + GetLengthSid(psid);', '        // max ACL size is USHRT_MAX', '        if (required_size > USHRT_MAX)', '            return PyErr_Format(PyExc_OverflowError, "%s: adding ACE would put ACL over size limit", __FUNCTION__ );', '        psacl_padded->AclSize = (unsigned short)required_size;']}
description: An integer overflow exists in pywin32 prior to version b301 when adding an access control entry (ACE) to an access control list (ACL) that would cause the size to be greater than 65535 bytes. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could crash the vulnerable process.

code_evidence: required_size is computed in unsigned short by adding psacl->AclSize, sizeof(SYSTEM_AUDIT_ACE), and a cast of GetLengthSid(psid); all operands are truncated to 16 bits, so the sum can wrap to a small value before malloc.
The wrapped required_size drives ZeroMemory and the memcpy of psacl->AclSize bytes, and is then stored into psacl_padded->AclSize; an undersized allocation can be overrun.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the size arithmetic wraps when the result exceeds the unsigned short range, and the truncated value is used as an allocation and copy size. This is distinct from a simple out-of-bounds write: the missing range check on the size computation is the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the ACL size calculation is performed in unsigned short, so adding an ACE to an ACL near 65535 bytes wraps the total to a small value. Trigger: AddAuditAccessAce returns ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED and the resize path allocates the wrapped size. Consequence: the subsequent memcpy and ACE insertion write beyond the undersized buffer, causing memory corruption or a crash (DoS).
