if ( *(next_opcode) != RE_OPCODE_LITERAL ||
(*(next_opcode) == RE_OPCODE_LITERAL &&
*(next_opcode + 1) == *next_input))

input += input_incr * repeat_any_args->min;
bytes_matched += repeat_any_args->min;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop advances next_input and dereferences it before validating the bound, and the post-loop increment of bytes_matched is not clamped. Trigger: a crafted file producing a repeat-any-ungreedy opcode with a large min/max causes next_input to point past the input buffer, so *next_input reads out-of-bounds memory, leading to over-read, crash, or information disclosure.

commit_msg: imgcodecs: remove assert() usage
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                            assert(0);', '            assert(0);'], 'added_lines': ['                            CV_Error(Error::StsInternal, "");', '            CV_Error(Error::StsInternal, "");']}
description: In OpenCV 3.3.1, an assertion failure happens in cv::RBaseStream::setPos in modules/imgcodecs/src/bitstrm.cpp because of an incorrect integer cast.

code_evidence: In the 1bpp byte-encoded path, decoded run length `len` is checked against the remaining line buffer; when the check fails the code calls `assert(0)` before jumping to `bad_decoding_1bpp`.
In the switch default for unsupported `m_bpp`, the function calls `assert(0)` unconditionally.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function contains assert() statements reachable from attacker-controlled image data, matching CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion), whose impact is DoS via application exit. The root cause is using assert for input validation rather than a recoverable error path; the consequence is process termination, not memory corruption.

evidence_lines.code:
default:
assert(0);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function trusts image header fields (`m_bpp`, `m_type`) and stream data. A crafted RLE run that overruns the line buffer, or an unsupported bit depth, reaches an assert() rather than returning a clean error. In builds with assertions enabled this aborts the process, so malformed input causes a crash instead of graceful failure.

commit_msg:
The rawmidi core allows user to resize the runtime buffer via ioctl,
and this may lead to UAF when performed during concurrent reads or
writes: the read/write functions unlock the runtime lock temporarily
during copying form/to user-space, and that's the race window.

This patch fixes the hole by introducing a reference counter for the
runtime buffer read/write access and returns -EBUSY error when the
resize is performed concurrently against read/write.

Note that the ref count field is a simple integer instead of
refcount_t here, since the all contexts accessing the buffer is
basically protected with a spinlock, hence we need no expensive atomic
ops.  Also, note that this busy check is needed only against read /
write functions, and not in receive/transmit callbacks; the race can
happen only at the spinlock hole mentioned in the above, while the
whole function is protected for receive / transmit callbacks.

Reported-by: butt3rflyh4ck <butterflyhuangxx@gmail.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/CAFcO6XMWpUVK_yzzCpp8_XP7+=oUpQvuBeCbMffEDkpe8jWrfg@mail.gmail.com
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/s5heerw3r5z.wl-tiwai@suse.de
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\t runtime->buffer + appl_ptr, count1)) {', '\t\t\t\treturn result > 0 ? result : -EFAULT;', '\t\t\t}', '\treturn result;'], 'added_lines': ['\tint err = 0;', '\tsnd_rawmidi_buffer_ref(runtime);', '\t\t\t\t\t runtime->buffer + appl_ptr, count1))', '\t\t\t\terr = -EFAULT;', '\t\t\tif (err)', '\t\t\t\tgoto out;', ' out:', '\tsnd_rawmidi_buffer_unref(runtime);', '\treturn result > 0 ? result : err;']}
description: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s implementation of MIDI, where an attacker with a local account and the permissions to issue ioctl commands to midi devices could trigger a use-after-free issue. A write to this specific memory while freed and before use causes the flow of execution to change and possibly allow for memory corruption or privilege escalation. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to confidentiality, integrity, as well as system availability.

code_evidence: The function takes the runtime spinlock at line 9, iterates over runtime->buffer while holding it, but at line 23 releases the lock to call copy_to_user from runtime->buffer + appl_ptr (lines 24-25) and reacquires it at line 28. During this unlocked window the pointer runtime->buffer and the appl_ptr offset are no longer protected, and the buffer can be freed/resized by a concurrent ioctl.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the code accesses memory through runtime->buffer + appl_ptr after the lock protecting that buffer's lifetime has been released, allowing a concurrent free to occur before the access. This is a lifetime/ordering flaw, not merely an out-of-bounds read, since the pointer itself becomes dangling.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the read path drops runtime->lock around copy_to_user while still holding a raw pointer into runtime->buffer and a cached appl_ptr. Trigger: a concurrent rawmidi resize ioctl frees/reallocates the runtime buffer during that unlocked window. Consequence: copy_to_user dereferences freed memory, causing a use-after-free that may corrupt memory or escalate privileges.

Security fixes: expect final changes for release 1.75.3.
* Fixed a debian security issue with fscanf() reading a string with
  possible buffer overflow.
* There were also a few similar situations with sscanf().
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['char     buf[L_BUF_SIZE];', '    ignore = fscanf(fp, "Rootname: %s\\n", buf);', '    ignores = fgets(buf, L_BUF_SIZE, fp);   /* Title: ... */', '    ignores = fgets(buf, L_BUF_SIZE, fp);   /* X axis label: ... */', '    ignores = fgets(buf, L_BUF_SIZE, fp);   /* Y axis label: ... */', '    ignore = fscanf(fp, "Commandfile name: %s\\n", buf);', '    ignore = fscanf(fp, "Output file name: %s\\n", buf);'], 'added_lines': ['char     buf[L_BUFSIZE];', '    ignore = fscanf(fp, "Rootname: %511s\\n", buf);  /* L_BUFSIZE - 1 */', '    ignores = fgets(buf, L_BUFSIZE, fp);   /* Title: ... */', '    ignores = fgets(buf, L_BUFSIZE, fp);   /* X axis label: ... */', '    ignores = fgets(buf, L_BUFSIZE, fp);   /* Y axis label: ... */', '    ignore = fscanf(fp, "Commandfile name: %511s\\n", buf);  /* L_BUFSIZE - 1 */', '    ignore = fscanf(fp, "Output file name: %511s\\n", buf);']}
description: Leptonica before 1.75.3 does not limit the number of characters in a %s format argument to fscanf or sscanf, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (stack-based buffer overflow) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a long string, as demonstrated by the gplotRead and ptaReadStream functions.

code_evidence: Line 4 declares a fixed-size stack buffer, buf[L_BUF_SIZE], which is the destination for multiple file-derived strings.

Lines 23-24 use an unbounded %s conversion in fscanf to read a Rootname token from the gplot file directly into buf; no maximum field width is specified, so a token longer than the buffer overflows the stack.
Lines 49-50 repeat the same unbounded %s read for Commandfile name into buf before stringReplace.
Lines 62-63 repeat the unbounded %s read for Output file name into buf.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes attacker-controlled file data past the end of the intended stack buffer buf, which is exactly an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). This is the direct memory-corruption cause; the %s format misuse is the mechanism, not merely an input-validation gap.

evidence_lines.code: char     buf[L_BUF_SIZE];

ignore = fscanf(fp, "Rootname: %s\n", buf);
rootname = stringNew(buf);

ignore = fscanf(fp, "Commandfile name: %s\n", buf);
stringReplace(&gplot->cmdname, buf);

ignore = fscanf(fp, "Output file name: %s\n", buf);
stringReplace(&gplot->outname, buf);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: fscanf format strings use %s without a width limit, so the number of bytes written into the fixed stack buffer buf is controlled by the input file. Trigger: a crafted gplot file containing an overlong Rootname, Commandfile name, or Output file name token. Consequence: stack-based buffer overflow, corrupting adjacent memory and potentially enabling crashes or code execution.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  OPJ_UINT32 crh = img->comps[2].h;', '  if (cbw != crw || cbh != crh)', '    return;', '  if (!sycc420_size_is_valid(yw, cbw) || !sycc420_size_is_valid(yh, cbh))', '    return;'], 'added_lines': ['  if (!sycc420_size_is_valid(img))', '    return;', '']}
description: fxcodec/codec/fx_codec_jpx_opj.cpp in PDFium, as used in Google Chrome before 50.0.2661.75, does not properly implement the sycc420_to_rgb and sycc422_to_rgb functions, which allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information from process memory or cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via crafted JPEG 2000 data in a PDF document.

code_evidence: Component widths/heights are read from comps[1] and comps[2]; the only constraints are cbw==crw, cbh==crh, and size validity of (yw,cbw)/(yh,cbh). Nothing ties crw/crh to yw/yh or bounds the cr chroma buffer relative to the luma buffer before the loops.
The chroma pointers cb and cr are taken from comps[1].data and comps[2].data, then dereferenced via *cb and *cr in the nested loops iterating over yh and yw.
In the trailing row branch, cb and cr are decremented when extw is set, then dereferenced, so the read index depends on the extw computation rather than a bounds check on the cr buffer.

In the trailing column branch, cb and cr are rewound by cbw and crw when exth is set, then dereferenced; if the chroma buffers are shorter than the luma-derived traversal, these reads exceed the allocated chroma data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-200 fits because the supported consequence is disclosure of process memory contents to an attacker through malformed JPEG 2000 input; the out-of-bounds read is the enabling mistake and information exposure is the resultant confidentiality impact. A pure crash-only framing would align with a memory-safety CWE, but here the read can expose sensitive data, matching the target label.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function walks the luma grid (yh*yw) while reading chroma buffers whose dimensions are only checked against each other, not against the luma size or allocated chroma data. Trigger: crafted JPEG 2000 data with mismatched/malformed component dimensions or subsampling causes the trailing-row/column rewind and loop dereferences to read past the chroma buffers. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds read of process memory, which can leak heap contents (and may crash).

description: In PHP versions 7.3.x below 7.3.27, 7.4.x below 7.4.15 and 8.0.x below 8.0.2, when using SOAP extension to connect to a SOAP server, a malicious SOAP server could return malformed XML data as a response that would cause PHP to access a null pointer and thus cause a crash.

Line 95 passes trav->name directly to soap_error1 with %s; libxml permits an element node with a NULL name (malformed XML from a malicious SOAP/WSDL server), so the format handler dereferences a NULL pointer. } else if (is_wsdl_element(trav) && !node_is_equal(trav,"documentation")) {
soap_error1(E_ERROR, "Parsing WSDL: Unexpected WSDL element <%s>", trav->name);

commit_msg:
Allowlist certain data types to avoid a seg fault.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 356326671
Change-Id: I23b65b52e93798cb5a6744632d31b0f88c6b6b31
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  OP_REQUIRES(context, dtype_ != DT_RESOURCE && dtype_ != DT_VARIANT,', '              errors::InvalidArgument(', '                  "Resource and variant dtypes are invalid for this op."));']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. Calling `tf.raw_ops.ImmutableConst`(https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/raw_ops/ImmutableConst) with a `dtype` of `tf.resource` or `tf.variant` results in a segfault in the implementation as code assumes that the tensor contents are pure scalars. We have patched the issue in 4f663d4b8f0bec1b48da6fa091a7d29609980fa4 and will release TensorFlow 2.5.0 containing the patch. TensorFlow nightly packages after this commit will also have the issue resolved. If using `tf.raw_ops.ImmutableConst` in code, you can prevent the segfault by inserting a filter for the `dtype` argument.

code_evidence: The constructor reads the dtype_ attribute via context->GetAttr(kDTypeAttr, &dtype_) and then proceeds to read shape_ without any validation of dtype_. The patch context shows the fix adds a guard rejecting DT_RESOURCE and DT_VARIANT before shape_ is read; in the original function no such constraint exists, so dtype_ may hold a non-scalar type.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-681 fits because the function permits a dtype whose in-memory representation is not a plain scalar, so the value is interpreted as a different type than it is. The missing dtype constraint is the incorrect type handling; the segfault is the downstream consequence, not the weakness itself.

evidence_lines.code:
OP_REQUIRES_OK(context, context->GetAttr(kDTypeAttr, &dtype_));
OP_REQUIRES_OK(context, context->GetAttr(kShapeAttr, &shape_));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function accepts an arbitrary dtype_ without restricting it to scalar types. Trigger: calling ImmutableConst with dtype tf.resource or tf.variant. The implementation then treats the tensor contents as pure scalars, producing a type-mismatched interpretation and a segfault (supported consequence).

commit_msg:
ares: Prevent buffer overlow in ares_parse_a_reply (CVE-2017-9454)

This buffer overflow is in the embedded copy of ares that will be
used unless the external alternative c-ares is used by specifying
the configure argument --with-c-ares.

It has been found with LibFuzzer from the LLVM project.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      if (aptr + rr_len > abuf + alen)', '\t{', '\t  free(rr_name);', '\t  status = ARES_EBADRESP;', '\t  break;', '\t}']}
description: Buffer overflow in the ares_parse_a_reply function in the embedded ares library in ReSIProcate before 1.12.0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds-read) via a crafted DNS response.

code_evidence: rr_len is taken from the untrusted DNS answer header via DNS_RR_LEN(aptr) at line 58, then aptr advances past the fixed RR header at line 59. The A-record branch at lines 60-64 reads sizeof(struct in_addr) bytes from aptr with memcpy without first confirming that aptr + rr_len lies within the abuf/alen buffer.

The only post-advance check is aptr += rr_len at line 80 followed by aptr > abuf + alen at line 81; this occurs after the read and permits aptr == abuf + alen, so a truncated answer can make the memcpy read past the buffer end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads memory past the intended buffer boundary, which is exactly CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read. It is not merely a write overflow because the unsafe operation is a read of address bytes; the later aptr > abuf + alen check is insufficient and occurs after the read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length field from an attacker-controlled DNS response is trusted for the A-record copy before any bounds check ties aptr + rr_len to abuf + alen. Trigger: a crafted response whose answer RR length/position places the address data at or beyond the buffer end. Consequence: an out-of-bounds read during memcpy, enabling remote denial of service (crash) and potential memory disclosure.

commit_msg: Make overflow not possible
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    const char * const dest_end = dest + dest_size;', '    if (dest + items_count * sizeof(T) > dest_end)'], 'added_lines': ['    if (static_cast<UInt64>(items_count) * sizeof(T) > dest_size)']}
description: ClickHouse is an open-source column-oriented database management system that allows generating analytical data reports in real-time. A heap buffer overflow issue was discovered in ClickHouse server. An attacker could send a specially crafted payload to the native interface exposed by default on port 9000/tcp, triggering a bug in the decompression logic of Gorilla codec that crashes the ClickHouse server process. This attack does not require authentication. This issue has been addressed in ClickHouse Cloud version 23.9.2.47551 and ClickHouse versions 23.10.5.20, 23.3.18.15, 23.8.8.20, and 23.9.6.20.

code_evidence: items_count is read from the untrusted source payload at line 7; the destination-size guard on lines 12-13 uses pointer arithmetic dest + items_count * sizeof(T) compared against dest_end.

The loop at line 22 iterates up to items_count and writes to dest at lines 45-46, advancing dest each iteration; if items_count * sizeof(T) overflows the pointer arithmetic check, the loop can write past dest_size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes attacker-influenced data into dest without a reliable upper bound, producing an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The fix replaces pointer arithmetic with a UInt64 multiplication compared to dest_size, confirming the overflow in the size check was the root cause rather than mere integer truncation alone.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the bounds check computes dest + items_count * sizeof(T), so a large attacker-controlled items_count can wrap the pointer arithmetic and bypass the comparison against dest_end. Trigger: a crafted Gorilla-compressed native-interface payload declaring an oversized item count. Consequence: the loop writes T values past the destination buffer, causing heap buffer overflow, crash, and potential memory corruption.

DO NOT MERGE omx: check buffer port before using

Bug: 28816827
Change-Id: I3d5bad4a1ef96dec544b05bb31cc6f7109aae0a5

description: omx/OMXNodeInstance.cpp in libstagefright in mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-08-01 does not validate the buffer port, which allows attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka internal bug 28816827.

code_evidence: findBufferHeader(buffer) returns a header without validating that the buffer belongs to the output port; the result is dereferenced immediately at lines 4-6.

The unvalidated header is inserted into mOutputBuffersWithCodec and passed to OMX_FillThisBuffer, so an attacker-supplied buffer id can drive a pointer not valid for the output port into codec operations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function operates on a memory buffer (header) without verifying it lies within the intended output-port boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds operation on a buffer. The missing port validation is the concrete cause enabling the out-of-bounds access, rather than a mere null-pointer issue.

OMX_BUFFERHEADERTYPE *header = findBufferHeader(buffer);
header->nFilledLen = 0;

mOutputBuffersWithCodec.add(header);
OMX_ERRORTYPE err = OMX_FillThisBuffer(mHandle, header);

commit_msg:
In case of error when adding a new rule that refers to an anonymous set,
deactivate expressions via NFT_TRANS_PREPARE state, not NFT_TRANS_RELEASE.
Thus, the lookup expression marks anonymous sets as inactive in the next
generation to ensure it is not reachable in this transaction anymore and
decrement the set refcount as introduced by c1592a89942e ("netfilter:
nf_tables: deactivate anonymous set from preparation phase"). The abort
step takes care of undoing the anonymous set.

This is also consistent with rule deletion, where NFT_TRANS_PREPARE is
used. Note that this error path is exercised in the preparation step of
the commit protocol. This patch replaces nf_tables_rule_release() by the
deactivate and destroy calls, this time with NFT_TRANS_PREPARE.

Due to this incorrect error handling, it is possible to access a
dangling pointer to the anonymous set that remains in the transaction
list.

Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tnf_tables_rule_release(&ctx, rule);'], 'added_lines': ['\tnft_rule_expr_deactivate(&ctx, rule, NFT_TRANS_PREPARE);', '\tnf_tables_rule_destroy(&ctx, rule);']}
description:
A use-after-free vulnerability was found in the Linux kernel's netfilter subsystem in net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c.

Mishandled error handling with NFT_MSG_NEWRULE makes it possible to use a dangling pointer in the same transaction causing a use-after-free vulnerability. This flaw allows a local attacker with user access to cause a privilege escalation issue.

We recommend upgrading past commit 1240eb93f0616b21c675416516ff3d74798fdc97.

code_evidence: When nf_tables_newexpr fails for an expression (e.g., a lookup referencing an anonymous set), control jumps to err_release_rule at line 134; the already-initialized expressions, including the one that took a reference to the anonymous set, remain linked in the rule.

The error path at line 187 calls nf_tables_rule_release, which releases the rule and its expressions without first deactivating the anonymous set in the transaction's next generation, leaving a dangling reference reachable via the transaction list.
The cleanup loop only module_puts expression ops that were not yet consumed (ops set to NULL at line 138), so it does not address the released anonymous set reference.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The freed anonymous set remains reachable through the transaction list, and subsequent lookups read that dangling pointer, matching CWE-416 use-after-free. A mere memory leak or refcount error would not involve reading previously freed memory.

evidence_lines.code:
err_release_rule:
nf_tables_rule_release(&ctx, rule);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path releases the partially built rule with nf_tables_rule_release instead of deactivating expressions under NFT_TRANS_PREPARE before destroying the rule. Trigger: adding a rule whose expression references an anonymous set fails during nf_tables_newexpr. The anonymous set stays referenced in the transaction list but is freed, so later lookup accesses freed memory (use-after-free).

commit_msg: Track number of pixels, not the number of runs
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if (count > xsize) {'], 'added_lines': ['    int x = 0;', '        if (x + count > xsize) {', '        x += count;']}
description: In libImaging/SgiRleDecode.c in Pillow through 7.0.0, a number of out-of-bounds reads exist in the parsing of SGI image files, a different issue than CVE-2020-5311.

code_evidence: Each iteration reads a control byte pixel from src and derives count; the bound check only compares the per-run count against xsize, not the accumulated number of pixels written across prior runs.
When RLE_COPY_FLAG is set, the loop reads *src++ count times; otherwise it reads one pixel then repeats it count times, advancing dest by z per pixel without any cumulative xsize limit.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads *src++ beyond the intended buffer when accumulated run lengths exceed xsize, matching CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read). Contrast with CWE-787: the defect is a read overrun of the source, not a write past dest.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the run-length guard at line 12 validates each run's count independently, so the sum of counts from successive runs can exceed xsize. Trigger: a crafted SGI RLE stream with multiple runs whose accumulated pixels exceed the row width. Consequence: the copy and literal branches read past the end of src, causing out-of-bounds reads.

commit_msg:
Fix heap buffer overflow in UnsortedSegmentSum.

When Index=int32, data_size and num_segments were truncated from int64 to int32. This truncation can produce negative numbers, which causes UnsortedSegmentFunctor to access out of bounds memory.

Also:
- Switches some indexing calculations to int64 to avoid signed integer overflow when either the input or output tensors have more than 2**31 - 1 elements.
- Fixes a range check error in the GPU kernel. The segment ID was checked against an upper bound measured in elements, not segments.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 256451663
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['void operator()(OpKernelContext* ctx, const Index num_segments,', '                  const TensorShape& segment_ids_shape,', '                  const Index data_size, const T* data,', '    const Index input_outer_dim_size = segment_ids.dimension(0);', '    const Index input_inner_dim_size = data_size / input_outer_dim_size;', '    TF_CHECK_OK(', '        GpuLaunchKernel(UnsortedSegmentCustomKernel<T, Index, ReductionF>,', '                        config.block_count, config.thread_per_block, 0,', '                        d.stream(), input_outer_dim_size, input_inner_dim_size,', '                        num_segments, segment_ids.data(), data, output.data()));'], 'added_lines': ['void operator()(OpKernelContext* ctx, const TensorShape& segment_ids_shape,', '                  typename TTypes<T, 2>::ConstTensor data,', '    const int64 data_size = data.size();', '    const int64 input_outer_dim_size = segment_ids.dimension(0);', '    const int64 input_inner_dim_size = data.dimension(1);', '    const int64 output_outer_dim_size = output.dimension(0);', '    TF_CHECK_OK(GpuLaunchKernel(', '        UnsortedSegmentCustomKernel<T, Index, ReductionF>, config.block_count,', '        config.thread_per_block, 0, d.stream(), input_outer_dim_size,', '        input_inner_dim_size, output_outer_dim_size, segment_ids.data(),', '        data.data(), output.data()));']}
description: In TensorFlow before 1.15, a heap buffer overflow in UnsortedSegmentSum can be produced when the Index template argument is int32. In this case data_size and num_segments fields are truncated from int64 to int32 and can produce negative numbers, resulting in accessing out of bounds heap memory. This is unlikely to be exploitable and was detected and fixed internally in TensorFlow 1.15 and 2.0.

code_evidence: The functor receives num_segments and data_size as Index (int32 when Index=int32), so 64-bit sizes are narrowed at the parameter boundary.
input_outer_dim_size and input_inner_dim_size are computed as Index; data_size / input_outer_dim_size can yield a truncated or negative inner dim size when data_size was already narrowed.
data_size drives GetGpuLaunchConfig and the kernel launch, which passes input_inner_dim_size and num_segments to UnsortedSegmentCustomKernel, so the narrowed values reach indexing math.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's int64-to-Index (int32) narrowing of data_size and num_segments is an incorrect conversion between numeric types whose unexpected negative values are used in indexing, matching CWE-681. The out-of-bounds access is the downstream consequence, not the weakness itself.

evidence_lines.code:
void operator()(OpKernelContext* ctx, const Index num_segments,
const Index data_size, const T* data,

const Index input_outer_dim_size = segment_ids.dimension(0);
const Index input_inner_dim_size = data_size / input_outer_dim_size;

config = GetGpuLaunchConfig(data_size, d);
num_segments, segment_ids.data(), data, output.data()));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: 64-bit element counts are converted to int32 Index parameters, which can truncate to negative values. Trigger: an oversized input where data_size or num_segments exceeds int32 range. The truncated inner-dim size and segment count then drive the GPU kernel's indexing, producing out-of-bounds heap access.

commit_msg:
x509: excessive resource use verifying policy constraints

A security vulnerability has been identified in all supported versions
of OpenSSL related to the verification of X.509 certificate chains
that include policy constraints.  Attackers may be able to exploit this
vulnerability by creating a malicious certificate chain that triggers
exponential use of computational resources, leading to a denial-of-service
(DoS) attack on affected systems.

Fixes CVE-2023-0464

Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Shane Lontis <shane.lontis@oracle.com>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/20568)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                                       last->anyPolicy, NULL) == NULL)'], 'added_lines': ['                                       last->anyPolicy, tree, 0) == NULL)']}
description:
A security vulnerability has been identified in all supported versions

of OpenSSL related to the verification of X.509 certificate chains
that include policy constraints.  Attackers may be able to exploit this
vulnerability by creating a malicious certificate chain that triggers
exponential use of computational resources, leading to a denial-of-service
(DoS) attack on affected systems.

Policy processing is disabled by default but can be enabled by passing
the `-policy' argument to the command line utilities or by calling the
`X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set1_policies()' function.

code_evidence: The loop iterates over each policy node in the previous level and calls tree_link_unmatched(curr, cache, node, tree), propagating the tree so descendant policy nodes can be linked while preserving resource-sharing context.
The anyPolicy node is added via ossl_policy_level_add_node using tree and flag 0 instead of NULL, so the new node is associated with the policy tree rather than created detached.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function is part of X.509 certificate chain policy validation; the fix ensures policy nodes are correctly linked within the verification tree, preventing resource-exhaustion during certificate validation. This directly concerns correct processing/validation of certificate contents (CWE-295), not a generic resource leak.

evidence_lines.code:
if (last->anyPolicy &&
ossl_policy_level_add_node(curr, cache->anyPolicy,
last->anyPolicy, NULL) == NULL)
return 0;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: During X.509 policy-constraint verification, the tree is now threaded through both unmatched-node linking and anyPolicy node creation. Without carrying the tree reference, node creation/linking could repeatedly duplicate or re-expand policy processing, causing exponential computational resource use when a malicious chain with policy constraints is verified. The supported consequence is denial of service during certificate chain validation.

commit_msg:
USB: fix out-of-bounds in usb_set_configuration

Andrey Konovalov reported a possible out-of-bounds problem for a USB interface
association descriptor.  He writes:
	It seems there's no proper size check of a USB_DT_INTERFACE_ASSOCIATION
	descriptor. It's only checked that the size is >= 2 in
	usb_parse_configuration(), so find_iad() might do out-of-bounds access
	to intf_assoc->bInterfaceCount.

And he's right, we don't check for crazy descriptors of this type very well, so
resolve this problem.  Yet another issue found by syzkaller...

Reported-by: Andrey Konovalov <andreyknvl@google.com>
Tested-by: Andrey Konovalov <andreyknvl@google.com>
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\tconfig->intf_assoc[iad_num] =', '\t\t\t\t\t(struct usb_interface_assoc_descriptor', '\t\t\t\t\t*)header;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tstruct usb_interface_assoc_descriptor *d;', '', '\t\t\td = (struct usb_interface_assoc_descriptor *)header;', '\t\t\tif (d->bLength < USB_DT_INTERFACE_ASSOCIATION_SIZE) {', '\t\t\t\tdev_warn(ddev,', '\t\t\t\t\t "config %d has an invalid interface association descriptor of length %d, skipping\\n",', '\t\t\t\t\t cfgno, d->bLength);', '\t\t\t\tcontinue;', '\t\t\t}', '', '\t\t\t\tconfig->intf_assoc[iad_num] = d;']}
description: drivers/usb/core/config.c in the Linux kernel before 4.13.6 allows local users to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read and system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted USB device, related to the USB_DT_INTERFACE_ASSOCIATION descriptor.

code_evidence: The USB_DT_INTERFACE_ASSOCIATION branch casts the raw descriptor header to usb_interface_assoc_descriptor and stores the pointer in config->intf_assoc[iad_num] without ever checking that header->bLength covers the full struct (bInterfaceCount and other fields). The only prior length check at [46,47] merely enforces bLength >= 2 and <= remaining size, so a truncated IAD descriptor is accepted and later dereferenced as a full structure.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts a descriptor without validating that its length covers the structure, so subsequent field accesses operate outside the intended buffer boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. A stricter length/struct-size check (as added by the patch) is the missing constraint.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the interface-association descriptor is trusted to be a complete usb_interface_assoc_descriptor based only on a minimal 2-byte header length check. Trigger: a crafted USB device supplies a short USB_DT_INTERFACE_ASSOCIATION descriptor; downstream consumers such as find_iad() read bInterfaceCount and other fields past the descriptor boundary, causing an out-of-bounds read and system crash/DoS.

commit_msg:
arm64: KVM: Sanitize PSTATE.M when being set from userspace

Not all execution modes are valid for a guest, and some of them
depend on what the HW actually supports. Let's verify that what
userspace provides is compatible with both the VM settings and
the HW capabilities.

Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Fixes: 0d854a60b1d7 ("arm64: KVM: enable initialization of a 32bit vcpu")
Reviewed-by: Christoffer Dall <christoffer.dall@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Mark Rutland <mark.rutland@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Dave Martin <Dave.Martin@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Marc Zyngier <marc.zyngier@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Will Deacon <will.deacon@arm.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tu32 mode = (*(u32 *)valp) & PSR_AA32_MODE_MASK;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tu64 mode = (*(u64 *)valp) & PSR_AA32_MODE_MASK;', '\t\t\tif (!system_supports_32bit_el0())', '\t\t\t\treturn -EINVAL;', '\t\t\tbreak;', '\t\t\tif (!vcpu_el1_is_32bit(vcpu))', '\t\t\t\treturn -EINVAL;', '\t\t\tbreak;', '\t\t\tif (vcpu_el1_is_32bit(vcpu))', '\t\t\t\treturn -EINVAL;']}
description: arch/arm64/kvm/guest.c in KVM in the Linux kernel before 4.18.12 on the arm64 platform mishandles the KVM_SET_ON_REG ioctl. This is exploitable by attackers who can create virtual machines. An attacker can arbitrarily redirect the hypervisor flow of control (with full register control). An attacker can also cause a denial of service (hypervisor panic) via an illegal exception return. This occurs because of insufficient restrictions on userspace access to the core register file, and because PSTATE.M validation does not prevent unintended execution modes.

code_evidence: set_core_reg accepts a userspace-supplied PSTATE value copied from uaddr at line 18. At lines 22-39 it extracts only the low mode bits (PSR_AA32_MODE_MASK) and checks them against a fixed allowlist of mode constants. The allowlist is unconditional: it accepts AArch32 modes (USR/FIQ/IRQ/SVC/ABT/UND) and AArch64 modes (EL0t/EL1t/EL1h) regardless of whether the guest is 32-bit or whether the hardware supports 32-bit EL0. No check ties the chosen mode to vcpu_el1_is_32bit(vcpu) or system_supports_32bit_el0().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function directly accepts untrusted userspace input and fails to validate that it satisfies required domain constraints (guest bitness and hardware support), matching CWE-20's improper validation of input properties. The missing constraint is validation, not sanitization/encoding, so CWE-20 fits rather than a transformation weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the PSTATE.M field supplied by userspace is validated against a static mode list without checking guest configuration or hardware capability. Trigger: a VM creator issues KVM_SET_ONE_REG for regs.pstate with a mode inconsistent with the vCPU (e.g., AArch32 mode on a 64-bit-only guest, or EL1 mode on a 32-bit guest). Consequence: the hypervisor later executes an illegal exception return or mode switch, allowing control-flow redirection or a hypervisor panic (DoS).

commit_msg:
If the device node of dvb_ca_en50221 is open() and the
device is disconnected, a UAF may occur when calling
close() on the device node.

The root cause is that wake_up() and wait_event() for
dvbdev->wait_queue are not implemented.

So implement wait_event() function in dvb_ca_en50221_release()
and add 'remove_mutex' which prevents race condition
for 'ca->exit'.

[mchehab: fix a checkpatch warning]

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-media/20221121063308.GA33821@ubuntu
